children.text: pāṇigrahe pulakitaṃ vapur aiśaṃ bhūtibhūṣitaṃ jayati
children.translated_text: Victorious is the body of <s>Aisa</s>, thrilled with horripilation at the taking of the hand and adorned with ash,
in which even <s>Manobhava</s>, though only a remainder of ashes, seems to sprout again.

children.text: mā vama saṃvṛṇu viṣam idam iti sātaṅkaṃ pitāmahenoktaḥ
children.translated_text: "Do not spew it out; hold in this poison," so <s>Pitamaha</s> said anxiously;
victorious at dawn is the bashful <s>Sambhu</s>, his lower lip blackened with collyrium.
Victorious is the enemy of <s>Smara</s>, wearing poison as a necklace at his throat at the end of his beloved's feet,
as though, when the arrows were uneven, he had entered for refuge with a sword tied at his neck.
Victorious is the eyelashed sidelong glance from the forehead of the moon-crested god, as he bows before his beloved,

children.text: dhanuṣi smareṇa nihitaḥ sakaṇṭakaḥ ketakeṣur iva ||
children.translated_text: like a thorny ketaka-arrow set by <s>Smara</s> upon his bow.
Victorious is <s>Sambhu</s>'s face: its filament is his matted hair, its honey is the <s>Ganga</s>, and its seed-pod is the circle of skulls,
a lotus born from the mud of the poison at his throat.
Not noticing that the water-offering of twilight is being drunk by the serpents that are his bracelets,
with his mind fixed on <s>Gauri</s>'s face, <s>Siva</s>, laughed at by <s>Vijaya</s>, is victorious.
Victorious is <s>Sambhu</s>'s water-offering, which slipped from his hand loosened by trembling as he looked at the reflected face of <s>Gauri</s>,
and which was being filled up by the weight of his sweat.
Victorious is <s>Siva</s>: the moon on him is sweetened by the twilight-redness of lac from the feet of his beloved, angry in love,
and his neck has become a touchstone for the gold of her bracelet.
Victorious is <s>Hara</s>'s crescent moon, a full moon of her nails, a doubled anklet, a chain of love,
among the toes and ankles of <s>Gauri</s>'s feet.
May the lotus-like eye of the lotus-eyed one, covered by <s>Sri</s>'s hand, bring you happiness,
as though it had come through the hollow of his navel to look at her hips.
Victorious is the dark chest of <s>Muradvis</s>, tawny with the saffron of <s>Sri</s>'s breasts,
which the sun-like radiance of the <s>Kaustubha</s> adorns, like the sky at the opening of day.
Victorious is the chest of <s>Madhubhid</s>, bearing the reflected body of his beloved and the <s>Kaustubha</s>,

children.text: puruṣāyitam abhyasyati lakṣmīr yad vīkṣya mukuram iva ||
children.translated_text: which <s>Lakshmi</s>, seeing it like a mirror, uses to practice the dominant lover's posture.
Victorious is the foot of <s>Muradvis</s>, by whose playful, moving toes <s>Lakshmi</s>'s navel is reached,

children.text: sa jayati yena kṛtā śrīr anurūpā padmanābhasya ||
children.translated_text: by which <s>Sri</s> was made fitting for <s>Padmanabha</s>.
May the line of hair on <s>Murari</s>, whose foremost part is attended by the <s>Srivatsa</s>,
remove your heat like the shadow of the lotus of his raised-stalk navel.

children.text: ādāya saptatantrocitāṃ vipañcīm iva trayīṃ gāyan
children.translated_text: Taking up the triple Veda as though it were a vina suited to the seven strings, and singing sweetly,
victorious is <s>Hari</s> with the horse-head proper to that music.

children.text: sa jayati mahābāho jalanidhijaṭhare ciraṃ nimagnāpi
children.translated_text: Victorious is the great-armed one by whom the earth, though long sunk in the belly of the ocean,

children.text: yenāntrair iva saha phaṇigaṇair balād uddhṛtā dharaṇī ||
children.translated_text: was forcibly raised up along with the hosts of serpents, as if along with entrails.
I praise <s>Janardana</s>, serpent-shaped, a potter for the cosmic egg,
on whose broad circle of hoods the earth bears the beauty of a clay bowl.
Victorious is <s>Candi</s>'s staff-like thigh when her beloved touches her foot with his head,
like a victory pillar of <s>Smara</s>, victorious even over <s>Sankara</s>.
Victorious is the face of the mountain's daughter, weary from taking the dominant lover's role,
by which even <s>Sambhu</s> appears like a lotus rising on the stalk of his navel.
Victorious are the breasts of the daughter of <s>Himagiri</s>, with her garment stolen by <s>Bahuleya</s>, who was anxious and suspected the elephant-faced one hidden in her lap,
while they are grasped by <s>Hara</s>'s smiling hands.
Victorious is that <s>Candi</s> at whose feet the moon-crested one, though fit for her neck, fell down, repelled by a mere humph,

children.text: yasyāś candraśikhaḥ smarabhallanibho jayati sā caṇḍī ||
children.translated_text: like an arrow of <s>Smara</s>.
Victorious is <s>Lakshmi</s>, with eyes bent crookedly in shame, laughed at by gods and demons,
when she placed the bridal garland on the god who bore the highly deceptive form of <s>Kaitabha</s>'s enemy.

children.text: tān asurān api harim api taṃ vande kapaṭakaiṭabhīrūpam
children.translated_text: I praise both those demons and <s>Hari</s> in that deceitful form of <s>Kaitabha</s>'s enemy,

children.text: yair yad bimbādharamadhulubdhaiḥ pīyūṣam api mumuce ||
children.translated_text: by whom, greedy for the honey of her bimba-red lower lip, even nectar was abandoned.
Victorious is the love-play of passion-blind <s>Sri</s>: the serpent was made a couch, <s>Garuda</s> was disregarded, and <s>Vidhi</s> was struck by her necklace,
while her breath was drunk by the hundred hoods.
Victorious is <s>Kamala</s>'s meditation on <s>Kaitabha</s>'s foe, as she takes the dominant lover's role,
her desire understood by smiling <s>Hari</s>, who knows gestures.
Victorious is <s>Vidhi</s> in the lotus of the navel, asleep from the cool spray of <s>Sri</s>'s breaths as she eagerly performs love-play with her beloved,
while the spread-out bees hum loudly.
Victorious, O one-tusked, two-mothered, beyond the three qualities, four-armed yet five-handed,
O son of the eight-bodied one, fragrant with saptacchada rut, praised by <s>Sanmukha</s>.
Sincerely worship the elephant-faced one, whose two temples are made of a pair of auspicious pitchers,
and from whose streams of rutting-fluid the bees hang swinging like balances for sesame.

children.text: yābhir anaṅgaḥ sāṅgīkṛtaḥ striyo 'strīkṛtāś ca tā yena
children.translated_text: By them <s>Ananga</s> was embodied, and by him women were made no women at all;
I bow to the two, <s>Kama</s> and his beloved, intent on leftward conduct.
I praise the anthill-born poet <s>Valmiki</s>, crooked like <s>Sakra</s>'s bow,

children.text: śakrāyudham iva vakraṃ valmīkabhuvaṃ kaviṃ naumi ||
children.translated_text: with dense ornamentation applied and shining with an array of varied colors.

children.text: vyāsagirāṃ niryāsaṃ sāraṃ viśvasya bhārataṃ vande
children.translated_text: I honor the <s>Bharata</s>, the extract of <s>Vyasa</s>'s utterances and the essence of the universe,

children.text: bhūṣaṇāyaiva sañjñāṃ yad aṅkitāṃ bhāratī vahati ||
children.translated_text: whose inscribed name <s>Bharati</s> bears simply as an ornament.
When the <s>Ramayana</s> exists, raising high the lineage of <s>Kakutstha</s>, what need is there of anything else?

children.text: rohati kulyā gaṅgāpūre kiṃ bahurase vahati ||
children.translated_text: Does a small irrigation channel rise, when the flood of the <s>Ganga</s> flows with abundant waters?
Alas, because of the fault of living too long, <s>Vyasa</s> stole his fame;

children.text: kair nocyeta guṇāḍhyaḥ sa eva janmāntarāpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who would not say that <s>Gunadhya</s> is that very man born in another life?
We bow to the poets of the blessed <s>Ramayana</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, and <s>Brhatkatha</s>;

children.text: trisrotā iva sarasā sarasvatī sphurati yair bhinnā ||
children.translated_text: through them <s>Sarasvati</s>, full of rasa, shines divided as if into three streams.
Mostly like the cooing in the throats of playful women, suggestive, sweet, and soft...
Even at the time of instruction, <s>Kālidāsa</s>'s sayings on the play of love are for delight.

children.text: bhavabhūteḥ sambandhād bhūdharabhūr eva bhāratī bhāti
children.translated_text: Because of his connection with <s>Bhavabhūti</s>, speech shines as the very daughter of the mountain.
If he has made her compassionate in this way, why else would a stone weep?

children.text: jātā śikhaṇḍinī prāg yathā śikhaṇḍī tathāvagacchāmi
children.translated_text: As <s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> formerly became <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, so I understand

children.text: prāgalbhyam adhikam āptuṃ vāṇī bāṇo babhūveti ||
children.translated_text: that speech became <s>Bāṇa</s> in order to acquire still greater boldness.

children.text: yaṃ gaṇayati guror anu yasyās te dharmakarma saṃkucitam
children.translated_text: After the teacher, I revere that father <s>Nīlāmbara</s>, whom she counts as <s>Uśanas</s> among poets,

children.text: kavim aham uśanasam iva taṃ tātaṃ nīlāmbaraṃ vande ||
children.translated_text: and whose rites of <s>dharma</s> and action are restrained.

children.text: sakalakalāḥ kalpayituṃ prabhuḥ prabandhasya kumudabandhoś ca
children.translated_text: The lord who can fashion all the arts of composition, and the friend of the lotus,
are one: king <s>Senakulatilaka</s> and the evening of the full moon.

children.text: kāvyasyākṣaramaitrībhājo na ca karkaśā na ca grāmyāḥ
children.translated_text: In poetry, words that possess the friendship of syllables are neither harsh nor vulgar;

children.text: śabdā api puruṣā api sādhava evārthabodhāya ||
children.translated_text: words, like men, are good men indeed when they make the meaning known.

children.text: vaṃśe ghuṇa iva na viśati doṣo rasabhāvite satāṃ manasi
children.translated_text: A fault does not enter the minds of good men, steeped in rasa, as a worm does not enter bamboo;

children.text: rasam api tu na pratīcchati bahudoṣaḥ saṃnipātīva ||
children.translated_text: but a man of many faults, like one afflicted with a disorder, does not accept even rasa.

children.text: viguṇo 'pi kāvyabandhaḥ sādhūnām ānanaṃ gataḥ svadate
children.translated_text: Even a composition defective in quality tastes sweet when it has reached the mouths of good men;
even a mere blowing sound, when repeated by fine bamboos, delights the ear.

children.text: svayam api bhūricchidraś cāpalam api sarvatomukhaṃ tanvan
children.translated_text: Though himself full of many holes, and spreading a restlessness facing every direction,
the slanderer, like a winnowing basket, is appointed to separate the chaff of fault.
For a composition that does not reveal meanings hidden within and is devoid of clarity,

children.text: sandarbhasya nadasya ca na rasaḥ prītyai rasajñānām ||
children.translated_text: as for a river that does not disclose what is concealed inside and is without clear water, there is no rasa to please connoisseurs of rasa.
Poetry, unfit to be frequented by the wicked, like nectar, arranged like gold,

children.text: surasārthamayaṃ kāvyaṃ triviṣṭapaṃ vā samaṃ vidmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and filled with the substance of the gods, or heaven itself: we know them to be equal.
When one is satisfied by the rice of words, husked clean by the winnowing fans that are the tongues of good poets,

children.text: tṛpto dayitādharam api nādriyate kā sudhā dāsī ||
children.translated_text: he does not even care for the beloved's lip; what, then, is nectar but a maidservant?
A good saying, though lacking recognized verbal ornament and though its placement of words slips in a favorable way,
delights like a woman going to a tryst, when its erotic mood is elevated.

children.text: adhvani padagrahaparaṃ madayati hṛdayaṃ na vā na vā śravaṇam
children.translated_text: On the road, something devoted to grasping the feet delights the heart, does it not, and the ear, does it not?
It is poetry in an assembly of connoisseurs, and an anklet at the time of play.
Only for one who has tasted the nectar-juice of the beloved's lip are good sayings sweet;
a cuckoo does not raise its soft note when the mango bud has not yet been tasted.
The young students of poetry study emotion as threaded by a girl's sidelong glance,
commented on by one third of an unchaste woman's eye, and explained by a female messenger.
<s>Govardhana</s>'s āryā verses, smooth in word and song and movement, going to rendezvous with the hearts of good people, rich in rasa,
are clear Upaniṣads of non-dual Love.
Speech, naturally suited to Prakrit rasa, has been forced into Sanskrit,
like the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s>, whose water suits low ground, led up to the sky.
Those bold-minded men by whom this <s>Āryāsaptaśatī</s> is disregarded

children.text: dūtīrahitā iva te na kāminīmanasi niviśante ||
children.translated_text: do not enter the minds of women, as men without a messenger do not.
Speech, though pure, if full of rasa, delights like a beloved stripped of her garment by the practice of love;

children.text: arasā sālaṅkṛtir api na rocate śālabhañjīva ||
children.translated_text: without rasa, even adorned with ornament, she does not please, like a wooden doll.
Their lives end with the appointed day; be gracious, let the wives of travelers live.
O row of watering-places, cover your breasts, mountains with paths hard to cross.
Very affectionate, well behaved, skilled in service, and agreeable to the mind,
the modest wife at once became so when the rival wife's breasts began to swell.
O <s>Kāverī</s>, noisy with waves whose bad conduct uproots the trees on your banks,
with mud rich in the leavings of cranes, before long you will become so.

children.text: ayi vividhavacanaracane dadāsi candraṃ kare samānīya
children.translated_text: O messenger, maker of many kinds of speeches, you bring the moon and place it in my hand;

children.text: vyasanadivaseṣu dūti kva punas tvaṃ darśanīyāsi ||
children.translated_text: but on days of distress, where again are you to be seen?

children.text: astu mlānir loko lāñchanam apadiśatu hīyatām ojaḥ
children.translated_text: Let there be fading; let the world allege a stain; let brilliance diminish.

children.text: tad api na muñcati sa tvāṃ vasudhāchāyām iva sudhāṃśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even so he does not abandon you, as the moon does not abandon the shadow of the earth.
Spreading excessive fickleness, entering within, and extremely hard,

children.text: mukharayasi svayam etāṃ sadvṛttāṃ śaṅkur iva ghaṇṭām ||
children.translated_text: you yourself make this virtuous woman sound out, like a peg striking a bell.
In the limbs of the young wagtail-pair only the expansion of Love grows old;
but play does not grow old on the disk of the earth, which holds treasures within.
Adopting blindness at the time for blindness and deafness at the time for deafness,
the lover of the two <s>Śrīkeśavas</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, is not a resident of the navel.

children.text: ayi koṣakāra kuruṣe vanecarāṇāṃ puro guṇodgāram
children.translated_text: O cocoon-maker, you proclaim the virtues of forest creatures in front of them;

children.text: yan na vidārya vicāritajaṭharas tvaṃ sa khalu te lābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that you have not been torn open and had your belly examined is indeed your gain.
Disregarding greatness, transgressing elders, without wealth or effort, hostile to nursing infants,
and bringing ill repute on what is dear: such is her passion for you, indifferent even to life.

children.text: aparādhād adhikaṃ māṃ vyathayati tava kapaṭavacanaracaneyam
children.translated_text: More than the offense itself, this composition of your deceitful words torments me;
the pain of a sword blow is not like the pain of being pierced by a needle.

children.text: asatīlocanamukure kim api pratiphalati yan manovarti
children.translated_text: Whatever in the mind is reflected in the mirror of an unchaste woman's eye,

children.text: sārasvatam api cakṣuḥ satimiram iva tan na lakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: even the eye of <s>Sarasvatī</s> does not perceive it, as though afflicted with darkness.

children.text: anyamukhe durvādo yaḥ priyavadane sa eva parihāsaḥ
children.translated_text: What is slander in another's mouth is the very same thing as jesting on a beloved's lips;
smoke born from other fuel is just smoke, but when born from aloe-wood it is incense.
O fortunate one, poor woman that she is, wandering about, trembling with curiosity, following fragrance,

children.text: tvayi mohāya varākī patitā madhupīva viṣakusume ||
children.translated_text: she fell upon you to her bewilderment, like a bee upon a poisonous flower.
O naive one, elephants are split apart merely by suspecting the scent of ichor;

children.text: upabhuñjate kareṇūḥ kevalam iha matkuṇāḥ kariṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in this world only bedbugs enjoy female elephants as elephants do with their trunks.
The bride, her body made small by excessive modesty, does not cross the threshold of the house.
But the safflower garden knows her boldness.

children.text: antargatair guṇaiḥ kiṃ dvitrā api yatra sākṣiṇo viralāḥ
children.translated_text: What use are inward qualities, where even two or three witnesses to them are rare?

children.text: sa guṇo gīter yad asau vanecaraṃ hariṇam api harati ||
children.translated_text: That is a true quality of song: it can carry away even a forest-roaming deer.

children.text: alulitasakalavibhūṣāṃ prātar bālāṃ vilokya muditaṃ prāk
children.translated_text: In the morning the rival wives first rejoiced to see the young woman with all her ornaments undisturbed.

children.text: priyaśirasi vīkṣya yāvakam atha niḥśvasitaṃ sapatnībhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But then, seeing red lac on the beloved's head, they sighed.
O bashful one, whose limbs are helpless after love through the deep night, sleeping happily,
open the petals of your lotus-eyes; your dawn has come.
Her face was not joined to mine, her breasts were not pressed against me, her hips and thighs were very far away;
by a hundred oaths I swear I was merely embraced by her arms.
This star-praising glance of yours, slender girl, is able to overstep the ears.

children.text: jinasiddhāntasthitir iva savāsanā kaṃ na mohayati ||
children.translated_text: Like adherence to the doctrine of the Jinas, attended by latent impressions, whom does it not bewilder?

children.text: alam aviṣayabhayalajjāvañcitam ātmānam iyam iyat samayam
children.translated_text: Enough: for so long she has cheated herself with fear, shame, and scruple where there was no real object for them.
Now, newly acquainted with her lover's virtues, she grieves and does not speak to her bed-companions.
In your absence, fierce and ruled by passion, she has been seized in body;
like <s>Gauri</s> by the enemy of <s>Tripura</s>, her fair body remains only half complete.
When the beloved is turned toward another, women who set their trust in a contrary current,

children.text: tadgatim icchantyaḥ sakhi bhavanti viphalaśramāḥ hāsyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: desiring to follow his course, friend, become ridiculous, their effort fruitless.

children.text: adhikaḥ sarvebhyo yaḥ priyaḥ priyebhyo hṛdi sthitaḥ satatam
children.translated_text: He who is dearer than all, dearer than the dear, and always lodged in the heart,

children.text: sa luṭhati virahe jīvaḥ kaṇṭhe'syās tvam iva sambhoge ||
children.translated_text: that life of hers rolls about in separation at her throat, as you do in union.

children.text: anayanapathe priye na vyathā yathā dṛśya eva duṣprāpe
children.translated_text: When the beloved is out of sight, the pain is not like that caused by one visibly hard to obtain.

children.text: mlānaiva kevalaṃ niśi tapanaśilā vāsare jvalati ||
children.translated_text: The sun-stone is merely faded at night, but by day it burns.
The lover, though not recognized even by a friend, delights her merely by his presence.

children.text: rahasi vyapadeśād ayam arthaḥ ivārājake bhogyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In secret, because of his assumed name, this treasure is to be enjoyed like property in a realm without a king.

children.text: aśrauṣīr aparādhān mama tathyaṃ kathaya manmukhaṃ vīkṣya
children.translated_text: You have heard of my offenses; look at my face and tell the truth.

children.text: abhidhīyate na kiṃ yadi na mānacaurānanaḥ kitavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why is nothing said, if the rogue has not the face of a thief of pride?

children.text: anyonyam anusrotasam anyad athānyat taṭāt taṭaṃ bhajatoḥ
children.translated_text: Following one another with the current, then each going from one bank to the other,
even when the sun has risen the young couple's bath in <s>Magha</s> is not finished.
O mango-creeper, your limbs bent with the weight of fruit, your fragrance blossoming everywhere,
marked by the potsherd of an outcaste, you, though fruitful, are indeed fruitless.

children.text: añjalir akāri lokair mlānim anāptaiva rañjitā jagatī
children.translated_text: People made obeisance with folded hands; the world was reddened before it had reached pallor.

children.text: sandhyāyā iva vasatiḥ svalpāpi sakhe sukhāyaiva ||
children.translated_text: Like the dwelling of twilight, even a short stay, friend, brings only happiness.

children.text: agṛhītānunayāṃ mām upekṣya sakhyo gatā bataikāham
children.translated_text: Alas, my friends have gone, leaving me alone and not accepting my plea for conciliation.

children.text: prasabhaṃ karoṣi mayi cet tvad upari vapur adya mokṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: If you use force against me, today I shall cast my body upon you.

children.text: asthirarāgaḥ kitavo mānī capalo vidūṣakas tvam asi
children.translated_text: You are inconstant in passion, a cheat, proud, fickle, a buffoon.

children.text: mama sakhyāḥ patasi kare paśyāmi yathā ṛjur bhavasi ||
children.translated_text: When you fall into my friend's hand, I shall see how straight you become.
Cruel one, this uninterrupted stream, showing water to a timid-hearted girl,

children.text: tvām anu dhāvati vimukhaṃ gaṅgeva bhagīrathaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: runs after you as you turn away, like the <s>Ganga</s> after <s>Bhagiratha</s>.
Because her nectar was held back by inward impurity, as by the tube of a sprinkler,

children.text: apy unmukhasya vihitā varavarṇini na tvayā tṛptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: even though I was turned upward, fair lady, you gave me no satisfaction.
O simple girl, between the very straight tree and the temple of the cheek of an elephant gladdened by rut,
their mutually charming exchange of fragrance tells of the rubbing.
Her glance, emerging openly through a tear in the cloth of the curtain made by her fingernails,
tastes sweet, stainless as it slips from the cloth, like a stream of nectar.
When she goes to her husband's house, her mother makes the path slippery with tears.

children.text: guṇagarvitā punar asau hasati śanaiḥ śuṣkaruditamukhī ||
children.translated_text: But she, proud of her virtues, smiles softly, her face dry from weeping.

children.text: aṅke niveśya kūṇitadṛśaḥ śanair akaruṇeti śaṃsantyāḥ
children.translated_text: When shall I, placing on my lap the girl with sidelong eyes as she says softly, 'You are cruel,'
loosen her braid with fingernails anointed with fragrant oil?
Enough, beautiful without adornment: you make ornament a subject of mockery for other women,
as a forest-tree creeper makes a flower a reproach to barren vines.

children.text: abudhā ajaṅgamā api kayāpi gatyā paraṃ padam avāptāḥ
children.translated_text: Even the foolish and motionless have somehow attained the highest place.

children.text: mantriṇa iti kīrtyante nayabalaguṭikā iva janena ||
children.translated_text: They are called ministers by people, like pills of policy-power.
Because of her extreme virtue's coolness, our friend is gentle in heat toward the world.
Her beloved, burning for a moment under her contrary mood, knows her heat.

children.text: anyāsv api gṛhiṇīti dhyāyann abhilaṣitam āpnoti
children.translated_text: Thinking 'housewife' even in other women, a man obtains what he desires,
just as one sees stone images as divinities.
Boy, without approaching low conduct, all around this deep and sweet

children.text: asyāḥ premṇaḥ pātraṃ na bhavasi sarito rasasyeva ||

children.translated_text: Command, insinuation, entreaty, reproach, laughter, and dry weeping:

children.text: iti nidhuvanapāṇḍityaṃ dhyāyaṃs tasyā na tṛpyāmi ||

children.text: ārdram api stanajaghanān nirasya sutanu tvayaitad unmuktam

children.text: āyāti yāti khedaṃ karoti madhu harati madhukarīvānyā
children.translated_text: Another comes and goes, causes weariness, takes honey like a bee;

children.text: adhidevatā tvam eva śrīr iva kamalasya mama manasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but you alone are the presiding deity of my mind, as <s>Śrī</s> is of the lotus.

children.translated_text: On reaching the southern quarter, the sun at once abandons the north;

children.text: ākṣipasi karṇam akṣṇā balir api baddhas tvayā tridhā madhye

children.text: muṣitāsmi tena jaghanāṃśukam api voḍhuṃ naśaktena ||

children.translated_text: Taking a large sum and giving away your garment, handsome man,

children.translated_text: to be grasped, lovely woman, like Love's own kingdom?

children.translated_text: the finger, handsome man, rests on reaching you, like reaching <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: ekaḥ sa eva jīvati svahṛdayaśūnyo 'pi sahṛdayo rāhuḥ
children.translated_text: That one <s>Rahu</s> alone lives, though empty-hearted and yet tender-hearted,

children.text: yaḥ sakalalaghimakāraṇam udaraṃ na bibharti duṣpūram ||
children.translated_text: who does not carry a hard-to-fill belly, the cause of every kind of meanness.

children.text: ekena cūrṇakuntalam apareṇa kareṇa cibukam unnamayan
children.translated_text: With one hand smoothing her powdered curls, and with the other lifting her chin,
I see her face at the city gate, its ears washed by tears.

children.text: ekaṃ jīvanamūlaṃ cañcalam api tāpayantam api satatam
children.translated_text: That poor woman carries you inside, as the nose carries breath,

children.text: antar vahati varākī sā tvāṃ nāseva niḥśvāsam ||
children.translated_text: the one root of life, though unsteady and though constantly burning.

children.text: ekaṃ vadati mano mama yāmi na yāmīti hṛdayam aparaṃ me
children.translated_text: My mind says one thing, 'I shall go'; my heart says another, 'I shall not go.'
A double heart is fitting for you, beautiful woman, since you have stolen your lover's heart.
With a bed of castor leaves, producing sweat, with her broad expanse of hips,
the ploughman's wife, meeting like a dust-poultice, removes the fever of Love.

children.text: kelinilayaṃ sakhīm iva nayati navoḍhāṃ svayaṃ na māṃ bhajate
children.translated_text: She herself leads the newly married woman to the house of play as if to a friend; she does not attend to me

children.text: itthaṃ gṛhiṇīm arye stuvati prativeśinā hasitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, noble lady, when the neighbor praised the housewife, there was laughter.
For the expectation was, 'This ketakī will become beautiful in its hollow with the passage of time,'

children.text: vṛddhir yathā yathā syās tathā tathā kaṇṭakotkarṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but as its growth increases, so too does the protrusion of its thorns.
Feigning sleep, listening to the sound of my breaths, why with your sharp breaths

children.text: vidhyasi māṃ niḥśvāsaiḥ smaraḥ śaraiḥ śabdavedhīva ||
children.translated_text: do you pierce me, like <s>Smara</s>, who strikes by sound, with his arrows?
Where is that silk garment of sloughed skin, and where is the row of serpent-jewels fit for ornament?
O <s>Yamunā</s>, after the departure of the serpent <s>Kāliya</s>, you have become accessible to everyone.

children.text: kiṃcinna bālayoktaṃ na saprasādā niveśitā dṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: The young girl said nothing at all, nor was a gracious glance cast down upon me;

children.text: mayi padapatite kevalam akāri śukapañjaro vimukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when I had fallen at her feet, only the parrot's cage was turned away.
With laughter made and hands clapped, while young men gazed with eyes restless from love,

children.text: kṣiptaḥ kṣipto nipatann aṅge nartayati bhṛṅgas tām ||
children.translated_text: the bee, falling again and again upon her body as it was flung away, made her dance.
Lotus-faced woman, even while making a prevention of mouths on every side, it adorns her:
the banks with blocked voices, and the rivers with restless eyes.
O cheat, she has been elaborately deceived by you, moving slowly from modesty;
even with many throws, now she does not come, like a piece in a dice game.
Who is of a praiseworthy birth, whose good fortune even on a winter night
this girdle-sound, long as a snowy wind, proclaims?

children.text: kim aśakanīyaṃ premṇaḥ phaṇinaḥ kathayāpi yā bibheti sma
children.translated_text: What is impossible for love? She who once trembled even at the mention of a serpent
now sleeps on the foam-pillow of the serpent on <s>Giriśa</s>'s arm.
For one robbed by courtesans through love, as though by counterfeit gold,
the distress of losing wealth seems slight; becoming a public laughingstock is great.

children.text: kiṃ parvadivasam ārjitadantoṣṭhi nijaṃ vapur na maṇḍayasi
children.translated_text: Why, with teeth and lips polished for a festival day, do you not adorn your own body?

children.text: sa tvāṃ tyajati na parvasv api madhurām ikṣuyaṣṭim iva ||
children.translated_text: He does not leave you even on festival days, like a sweet sugarcane stalk.

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ sāhasakāriṇi tava nayanārdhena so 'dhvani spṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Alas, rash woman: that ascetic of yours was touched on the road by half of your eye;

children.text: upavītād api vidito na dvijadehas tapasvī te ||
children.translated_text: though his twice-born body was known even by the sacred thread, he was no ascetic after that.
Even while pain is being drawn out, this meeting delights me indeed,
like a rain of heavenly Ganges water from a fierce, cloudless sky.

children.text: kūpaprabhavāṇāṃ param ucitam apāṃ paṭṭabandhanaṃ manye
children.translated_text: For waters born from a well, I think the binding with a cloth is most fitting,

children.text: yāḥ śakyante labdhuṃ na pārthivenāpi viguṇena ||
children.translated_text: since they cannot be obtained even by a king, if he lacks qualities.
Nail-tips sunk in your hand, having wandered and rested, night hard to obtain,

children.text: ravir iva yantrollikhitaḥ kṛśo 'pi lokasya harasi dṛśam ||
children.translated_text: though lean, you steal people's gaze like the sun engraved by a machine.

children.text: kiṃ karavāṇi divāniśam api lagnā sahajaśītalaprakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: What shall I do? Day and night I cling, naturally cool by nature;

children.text: hanta sukhayāmi na priyam ātmānam ivātmanaś chāyā ||
children.translated_text: alas, I do not please my beloved, like one's own shadow does not please oneself.
If the weight of hair is on the head, if death comes from falling into a pool of nectar,

children.text: dayitavahanena vakṣasi yadi bhāras tad idam acikitsyam ||
children.translated_text: if the burden lies on the breast from carrying the beloved, then this condition is incurable.

children.text: kiṃcitkarkaśatām anu rasaṃ pradāsyan nisargamadhuraṃ me
children.translated_text: Since it will give me flavor, natural sweetness, after a little roughness,

children.text: ikṣor iva te sundari mānasya granthir api kāmyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the knot of your anger, beautiful woman, is desirable, like that of sugarcane.

children.text: kena giriśasya dattā buddhir bhujagaṃ jaṭāvane'rpayitum
children.translated_text: Who gave <s>Giriśa</s> the idea of placing a serpent in the forest of his matted hair,
by which the pulling of his hair by the beloved's hand in the frenzy of love was stolen away?
Without thinking of blows from hands, feet, girdle, and necklace, with her hair seized by force,
the lover kisses his beloved's face, with trembling lip and reddened eyes.

children.text: kurutāṃ cāpalam adhunā kalayatu surasāsi yādṛśī tad api
children.translated_text: Let her now be fickle; let her be, good-tasting one, whatever she is; even so,
beautiful woman, after a harītakī she is like a stream of water drunk afterward.
With your moon-face stained by a collyrium mark, with drops of water fallen on your hair,
which man, cotton for the fresh fire of separation, is to be kept alive by you?

children.text: kṛcchrānuvṛttayo 'pi hi paropakāraṃ tyajanti na mahāntaḥ
children.translated_text: For great beings do not abandon helping others, even when their livelihood is hard to maintain;
elephants, though living on mere grass, have trunks wet with the fluid of giving.

children.text: kiṃ hasatha kiṃ pradhāvatha kiṃ janam āhvayatha bālakā viphalam
children.translated_text: Why do you laugh, why run, why call people, children, in vain?

children.text: tad atha darśayati yathāriṣṭaḥ kaṇṭhe'munā jagṛhe ||
children.translated_text: Then he shows how, as predicted, he was seized by the neck by this one.
Her eyes are soft and sweet with fear, sidelong cries, love, shame, and anger;

children.text: yoktuṃ na moktum athavā valate'sāv arthalabdharatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: having found pleasure in the object obtained, she turns neither to yoke him nor to release him.

children.text: ketakagarbhe gandhādareṇa dūrād amī drutam upetāḥ
children.translated_text: In their regard for fragrance, these bees quickly approached from afar to the heart of the ketakī;
like horses of <s>Madana</s>'s chariot, they take up the dust.

children.text: ko vakrimā guṇāḥ ke kā kāntiḥ śiśirakiraṇalekhānām
children.translated_text: What crookedness is there, what virtues, what radiance, in the streaks of the cool-rayed moon,
within which, after entering, a particular beast has taken possession?
Having made many efforts at churning, the lord, to defeat gods and demons,

children.text: icchati saubhāgyam adāt svayaṃvareṇa śriyaṃ viṣṇuḥ ||
children.translated_text: desired good fortune and took <s>Śrī</s> by self-choice, <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself.
Why, daughter, do you sleep among the new clouds, mistaking them for cheek-like rocks?
Experience the confusions of other lands, with flashing lightning-sport and thunder.

children.text: kāntaḥ padena hata iti saralām aparādhya kiṃ prasādayatha
children.translated_text: Why, after offending the simple girl by saying, 'The beloved was struck by her foot,' do you try to appease her?

children.text: so 'py evam eva sulabhaḥ padaprahāraḥ prasādaḥ kim ||
children.translated_text: If even he is so easily gained, is a foot-blow a favor?

children.text: karṇagateyam amoghā dṛṣṭis tava śaktir indradattā ca
children.translated_text: This unfailing glance of yours has gone to the ear, and your spear was given by <s>Indra</s>;
it has nowhere failed to win victory, nor has it fallen without purpose.

children.text: kleśayasi kim iti dūtīr yad aśakyaṃ sumukhi tava kaṭākṣeṇa
children.translated_text: Why do you trouble messengers, fair-faced woman, when what is impossible for your sidelong glance

children.text: kāmo 'pi tatra sāyakam akīrtiśaṅkī na saṃdhatte ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Kāma</s>, fearing disgrace, does not fit an arrow to that target?

children.text: ko veda mūlyam akṣadyūte prabhuṇā paṇīkṛtasya vidhoḥ
children.translated_text: Who knows the value of the moon staked by the lord in a game of dice,

children.text: prativijaye yat pratipaṇam adharaṃ gharanandinī vidadhe ||
children.translated_text: when at each victory the mistress of the house placed her lower lip as the counter-stake?

children.text: kupitāṃ caraṇapraharaṇabhayena muñcāmi na khalu caṇḍi tvām
children.translated_text: Angry woman, I certainly do not let you go out of fear of a blow from your foot,
for the bee resorts to the vine, enduring the strikes of leaves made fickle by the wind.
Beloved, when your brow is drawn tight in anger like <s>Smara</s>'s bow, restrain, as they fall,
the drops of tear-water dark with collyrium, like bees from a bow whose string has snapped.

children.text: kāmenāpi na bhettuṃ kimu hṛdayam apāri bālavanitānām
children.translated_text: If even <s>Kama</s> could not pierce the hearts of young women, how could anyone else?
For their breast seems swollen, as if from the blow of his blunt arrows.

children.text: kiṃ parajīvair dīvyasi vismayamadhurākṣi gaccha sakhi dūram
children.translated_text: Why do you sport with other men's lives, wonder-sweet-eyed friend? Go far away.
Let the snake-charmer play without hindrance with the snake in the courtyard.
As the beloved, her eyes trembling with anger, strikes his limbs with hand and foot,

children.text: roṣayati paruṣavacanais tathā tathā preyasīṃ rasikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so, by means of harsh words, the connoisseur of love excites his sweetheart more and more.

children.text: kas tāṃ nindati lumpati kaḥ smaraphalakasya varṇakaṃ mugdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Who blames her? Who, foolishly, wipes away the pigment from Love's tablet?

children.text: ko bhavati ratnakaṇṭakam amṛte kasyārucir udeti ||
children.translated_text: Who treats a jewel-thorn as a thorn, or in whom does distaste arise for nectar?
When you, angry woman, move about like a mango shoot restless with the play of your hand,

children.text: karakampitakaravāle smara iva sā mūrchitā sutanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: that slender woman faints, as if <s>Smara</s> himself were moving with a sword shaken in his hand.
Enough of family propriety; I love her. <s>Smara</s> bears witness, like a mongoose,
and for me, loving her by meditating on her, a slip of family-name is unavoidable.

children.text: kuta iha kuraṅgaśāvaka kedāre kalam amañjarīṃ tyajasi
children.translated_text: Why, young antelope, do you abandon the rice-blossom in this field?
This deceitful man is made of grass: his arrows are grass, his bow is grass.

children.text: khalasakhyaṃ prāṅ madhuraṃ vayo 'ntarāle nidāghadinam ante
children.translated_text: Friendship with a wicked man is sweet at first, like a summer day in the middle of life, but at the end;
friendship with good people is lovely in its beginning, middle, and conclusion.

children.text: guṇam adhigatam api dhanavān na cirān nāśayati rakṣati daridraḥ
children.translated_text: A rich man soon destroys even a quality he has acquired; a poor man preserves it.

children.text: majjayati rajjum ambhasi pūrṇaḥ kumbhaḥ sakhi na tucchaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A full jar, friend, sinks a rope in water; an empty one does not.

children.text: gurur api laghūpanīto na nimajjati niyatam āśaye mahataḥ
children.translated_text: Even something heavy, if brought into contact with lightness, surely does not sink in a great receptacle,
just as a mountain brought by the wind does not sink in the ocean, the abode of makaras.

children.text: gaurīpater garīyo garalaṃ gatvā gale jīrṇam
children.translated_text: For the husband of <s>Gauri</s>, even the very heavy poison, once it reached his throat, was digested there;

children.text: jīryati karṇe mahatāṃ durvādo nālpam api viśati ||
children.translated_text: but in the ears of the great, slander is digested; even a little of it does not enter.
Before her husband, the young woman, by a feigned tale, describes the adulterer as afflicted by Love,

children.text: prīṇayati pīḍayati ca bālā niḥśvasya niḥśvasya ||
children.translated_text: and, sighing again and again, she both delights him and torments him.
Let the elephant, surpassing excellent young women in gait, make his temples dark with rut-fluid.
O small-bellied one, mere elephant by the tying of your face, why do you carry rut-pride?
Hearing from the housewife the sulk caused by the offense of a slipped family-name,

children.text: snigdhāṃ priye sagarvāṃ sakhīṣu bālā dṛśaṃ diśati ||
children.translated_text: the girl casts among her friends a tender yet proud glance toward her beloved.
In this summer season, look at what has been made at the foot of the pleasure-grove:
it is as if coolness itself, under the pretext of the circular tree-basin, were coiled there in full.

children.text: guṇabaddhacaraṇa iti mā līlāvihagaṃ vimuñca sakhi mugdhe
children.translated_text: Do not release the pet bird, foolish friend, thinking, 'Its feet are bound by a string.'
On this branch encircled around it, the restraint of the cord will snap in a moment.
Before those whose ears and eyes are shut by fear of the deep lightning and great thunder,

children.text: bālā cumbati jāraṃ vajrād adhiko hi madaneṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the girl kisses her lover; for Love's arrow is stronger than the thunderbolt.

children.text: gṛhiṇīguṇeṣu gaṇitā vinayaḥ sevā vidheyateti guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Among a housewife's virtues are counted modesty, service, obedience, and such qualities;
but pride, mastery, and contrariness are the ornaments of women with lovely eyes.

children.text: guṇam āntaram aguṇaṃ vā lakṣmīr gaṅgā ca veda hariharayoḥ
children.translated_text: Whether the inner quality is a virtue or a defect, <s>Lakshmi</s> and <s>Ganga</s> know it in <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: ekā pade'pi ramate na vasati nihitā śirasy aparā ||
children.translated_text: One delights even at his foot; the other, though placed on his head, does not remain there.

children.text: gatvā jīvitasaṃśayam abhyastaḥ soḍhum aticirād virahaḥ
children.translated_text: After going to the danger of life, separation has at long last been trained to be endured.

children.text: akaruṇaḥ punar api ditsasi suratadurabhyāsam asmākam ||
children.translated_text: Cruel one, do you again wish to give us the hard-to-learn practice of love-making?
Even to the question about the slip of a family-name, after giving an answer chilled by excessive good conduct,

children.text: niḥśvasya mogharūpe svavapuṣi nihitaṃ tayā cakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: she sighed and fixed her gaze on her own body, useless in its beauty.
O bee, scent-seeker, your whole body was once set in the resin opened by the sal tree,
and now, after enjoying a hundred trees whose brows were released, you no longer wander.

children.text: guruṣu militeṣu śirasā praṇamasi laghuṣūnnatā sameṣu samā
children.translated_text: Among the heavy you bow your head; among the light you rise high; among equals you are equal.

children.text: ucitajñāsi tule kiṃ tulayasi guñjāphalaiḥ kanakam ||
children.translated_text: O scale, you know what is fitting; why do you weigh gold against gunja-berries?
Being carried away by the housewife and held back in front by the new bride,

children.text: mama naukādvitayārpitaguṇa iva hṛdayaṃ dvidhā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: my heart becomes split in two, like a rope fastened to two boats.
One string fit for drawing, like a bowstring, is enough for gaining a hundred thousand;

children.text: lūtātantubhir iva kiṃ guṇair vimardāsahair bahubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: what use are many strings, like spider-threads, unable to endure rubbing?

children.text: gāyati gīte vaṃśe vādayati sa vipañcīṣu
children.translated_text: He sings in song, he plays upon the flute and on the lutes,
and teaches the cage-parrot, beautiful woman, the syllables of your message.

children.text: gaṇayati na madhuvyayam ayam aviratam āpibatu madhukaraḥ kumudam
children.translated_text: This bee does not count the expenditure of honey; let him drink the night-lotus without ceasing.
The moon, proud of good fortune, merely envies the sun.

children.text: guṇavidhṛtā sakhi tiṣṭhasi tathaiva dehena kiṃ tu hṛdayaṃ te
children.translated_text: Held by the cord, friend, you remain just so with your body; but your heart
has been carried off by him, like the fragrance of a garland by the wind.

children.text: gurusadane nedīyasi caraṇagate mayi ca mūkayāpi tayā
children.translated_text: When I had fallen at her feet, close by in the elder's house, even though she was silent,

children.text: nūpuram apāsya padayoḥ kiṃ na priyam īritaṃ priyayā ||
children.translated_text: by taking the anklet from her feet, what dear thing was not uttered by my beloved?

children.text: granthilatayā kim ikṣoḥ kim apabhraṃśena bhavati gītasya
children.translated_text: What harm is a knotted vine to sugarcane? What is a Prakrit form to a song?

children.text: kim anārjavena śaśinaḥ kiṃ dāridryeṇa dayitasya ||
children.translated_text: What is lack of straightness to the moon? What is poverty to a beloved?
Even though the housewife, at the moment of seizing my hair, had closed her eyes with a hiss,
seeing the young girl's cheek bristle with joy, I was planted on the head by her foot.
Somehow this eye turns, heavy-lashed, red from wakefulness, with its pupils rolling,
its brow crooked in anger caused by the clear setting-in of nail-marks.
Though she is embracing him, with hips joined, with full thighs pressed, and the whole weight of her breasts laid upon him,

children.text: āliṅganty api bālā vadaty asau muñca muñceti ||
children.translated_text: the young woman says, 'Let go, let go!'

children.text: ghaṭitapalāśakapāṭaṃ niśi niśi sukhino hi śerate padmāḥ
children.translated_text: The happy lotuses sleep night after night with the doors of their petals closed;

children.text: ujjāgareṇa kairava kati śakyā rakṣituṃ lakṣmīḥ ||
children.translated_text: O night-lotus, how many fortunes can be guarded by staying awake?
Women deceived by their lovers reel about, and so do the flames of lamps when their oil has run out;
at dawn the hearts of travelers' wives burst, and so do the lotuses.
Seeing the head of her fickle beloved with hair marked by greyness,
the housewife felt only joy, even at a time fit for distress.

children.text: caṇḍi prasāritena spṛśan bhujenāpi kopanāṃ bhavatīm
children.translated_text: Fierce woman, though I touch you with an outstretched arm while you are angry,

children.text: tṛpyāmi paṅkilām iva piban nadīṃ nalinanālena ||
children.translated_text: I am satisfied as if drinking a muddy river through a lotus-stalk.
Abandoned after being enjoyed by a restless female serpent, cool and fragrant-bearing, wandering at night,
go, O ever-arriving dawn-wind, to fill the western quarter.
Long-traveling man, now the gazelle-eyed woman's gaze is like the <s>Karatoyā</s>, always full of water,
knotty with masses of moss-like creepers, her long meeting locks of hair.
Fierce woman, I was so intent only on looking at your thighs, revealed by the slightly restless garment,

children.text: dhūlibhayād api na mayā caraṇahṛtau kuñcitaṃ cakṣuḥ ||
children.translated_text: that, even from fear of dust, I did not contract my eye when taking your feet.
Her gait steals this heart: her earrings tremble, her curls move, her garment slips from her hard breasts, her pair of thighs is beautiful,
and her eyes are half closed from the fatigue caused by the weight of her hips.

children.text: caraṇaiḥ parāgasaikatam aphalam idaṃ likhasi madhupa ketakyāḥ
children.translated_text: Bee, you scratch this useless pollen-sand with your feet from the ketakī;
here, in this essence of beauty, there is no honey-river, not even water within.
Long-time traveler, simple man, why do you look with eyes rippling with suspicion?
This is the row of scars and calluses on her from embracing your sword.

children.text: capalāṃ yathā madāndhaś chāyāmayam ātmanaḥ karo hanti
children.translated_text: Just as a rut-blind elephant strikes with his trunk his own shadow, as though it were a restless female elephant,

children.text: āsphālayati karaṃ pratigajas tathāyaṃ puro ruddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so this rival elephant, blocked in front, beats his trunk against it.
Remembering that pair of her thighs, the tying-post for the elephant of my heart,
with its saffron stolen by her lower lip greedy for kisses, I am not satisfied.
Though the young woman has turned away, her neck bent sideways as she spreads out her hair,
she looks at you through the opening in her hair made by her fingers.
You cast an eye whose collyrium-price has been taken away by kissing, and whose redness from wakefulness is clear;
why at dawn, anxious from separation, like half an arrow of <s>Kāma</s>?

children.text: chāyāgrāhī candraḥ kūṭatvaṃ satatam ambujaṃ vrajati
children.translated_text: The moon grasps only a shadow, and the lotus continually goes to falsehood;
abandoning both, people in the assembly praise only your face.
Though I am downcast, seeing only a shadow, yet with courage risen high,
like a crowned archer striking <s>Rādhā</s>'s discus, she pierces my heart with skill.

children.text: jalabindavaḥ katipaye nayanād gamanodyame tava skhalitāḥ
children.translated_text: A few drops of water slipped from your eyes as you prepared to depart;

children.text: kānte mama gantavyā bhūr etair eva picchilitā ||
children.translated_text: beloved, the ground that I must traverse has been made slippery by these alone.
I remember her face, its cheeks pressed by earrings restrained by the pair of arms lifted in a yawn,
its languid gaze, its collyrium blurred by drops of water.

children.text: jāgaritvā puruṣaṃ paraṃ vane sarvato mukhaṃ harasi
children.translated_text: Having kept a man awake all night, you seize one facing every direction in the forest;

children.text: ati śaradanurūpaṃ tava śīlam idaṃ jātiśālinyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: this conduct of yours, O jasmine-vine, is very much in keeping with autumn.
With the jingling of bracelets, tosses of the hands, leaning against pillars, and silences,
beautiful woman, you adorn the doorway of the house even with dry weeping.

children.text: ḍhakkām āhatya madaṃ vitanvate kariṇa iva ciraṃ puruṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Men, like elephants, beat the drum and spread their rut for a long time;

children.text: strīṇāṃ kariṇīnām iva madaḥ punaḥ svakulanāśāya ||
children.translated_text: but the rut of women, like that of female elephants, brings destruction to their own family.

children.text: tāṃ tāpayanti manmathabāṇās tvāṃ prīṇayanti bata subhaga
children.translated_text: Love's arrows torment her, but they delight you, alas, fortunate man;
the sun's rays set fire to the sun-stone, but sweeten the moon.
Slender woman, by gaining your mountain slope, whose hip-slope is reddened by many mineral colors,
as by gaining the ground of a great mountain, I reach heaven by two fingers' breadth.

children.text: tyakto muñcati jīvanam ujhati nānugrahe'pi lolutvam
children.translated_text: When rejected he gives up his life; when favored he does not abandon his greediness.

children.text: kiṃ prāvṛṣeva padmākarasya karaṇīyam asya mayā ||
children.translated_text: What am I to do with this lotus-bed, as with the rainy season?
In the disaster of separation from you, the slender woman is pale and recognizable only by her shadow,
like a female swan in moonlight, fortunate man.

children.text: tvayi viniveśitacittā subhaga gatā kevalena kāyena
children.translated_text: Her mind fixed on you, fortunate man, she has gone only with her body,
like a river whose fish are blocked by a mass of clouds, gone only with its water.

children.text: tvayi saṃsaktaṃ tasyāḥ kaṭhoratara hṛdayam asamaśarataralam
children.translated_text: Her heart, harder than hard and trembling from the unequal-arrowed god, is attached to you;
like a wind-shaken garment-edge, it has split open from contact with thorns.

children.text: tvam asūryaṃpaśyā sakhi padam api na vināpavāraṇaṃ bhramasi
children.translated_text: Friend, you who do not see the sun wander not even a step without covering;

children.text: chāye kim iha vidheyaṃ muñcanti na mūrtimantas tvām ||
children.translated_text: O shadow, what is to be done here? Embodied beings do not leave you.
In separation from you, when the nights are lengthened and hatred of moon and sandal has arisen,

children.text: bisinīva māghamāse vinā hutāśane sā dagdhā ||
children.translated_text: she is burned like a lotus-stalk in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, even without fire.
Young woman, your crookedly acting rival wife, though distressed with grief, does not drink

children.text: kuṭilacaritā sapatnī na pibati bata śokavikalāpi ||
children.translated_text: the cluster of blooming aśoka buds struck by your foot.

children.text: talpe prabhur iva gurur iva manasijatantre śrame bhujiṣyeva
children.translated_text: On the bed she is like a master; in the treatise of Love, like a teacher; in exertion, like a servant woman;

children.text: gehe śrīr iva gurujanapurato mūrteva sā vrīḍā ||
children.translated_text: in the house, like Fortune; before the elders, like shame embodied.

children.text: tvam alabhyā mama tāvan moktum aśaktasya saṃmukhaṃ vrajataḥ
children.translated_text: So long as you are unattainable to me, as I am unable to let go and go forward to meet you...
like a shadow withdrawing, until you are no longer stopped by the wall.

children.text: tapasā kleśita eṣa prauḍhabalo na khalu phālgune'py āsīt
children.translated_text: This one, tormented by austerity, has grown strong and mature; truly he was not so even in <s>Phālguna</s>.

children.text: madhunā pramattam adhunā ko madanaṃ mihiram iva sahate ||
children.translated_text: Who now can endure <s>Madana</s>, maddened by spring honey, any more than the sun?
Fortunate man, with pale streaks marking the count of the days since your departure,
even the wall of her house has turned pale, like her cheek.
Friend, by the crooked, tender, sweet glance of that unvillage-like man,

children.text: viddhā tadekaneyā potriṇa iva daṃṣṭrayā dharaṇī ||
children.translated_text: I have been pierced, as the earth, destined for him alone, by the tusk of the Boar.

children.text: tvayi kugrāmavaṭadruma vaiśravaṇo vasatu vā lakṣmīḥ
children.translated_text: O bad-village banyan tree, whether <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> or Fortune herself dwell in you,
your only protection from the blows of rustic axes is the head of a buffalo.

children.text: tava mukhara vadanadoṣaṃ sahamānā moktum akṣamā sutanuḥ
children.translated_text: Slender woman, enduring the fault of your talkative mouth and unable to let you go,

children.text: sā vahati viṭa bhavantaṃ ghuṇamantaḥ śālabhañjīva ||
children.translated_text: she bears you, libertine, like a wooden doll carrying a worm inside.

children.text: tṛṇamukham iva na khalu tvāṃ tyajanty amī hariṇa vairiṇaḥ śabarāḥ
children.translated_text: Deer, these hostile Śabara hunters do not abandon you as though you were mere grass in their mouths.
With your antlers joined for battle, abandon this life, which consists only in fame.

children.text: tripuraripor iva gaṅgā mama mānini janitamadanadāhasya
children.translated_text: Proud woman, for me, whose burning from love has arisen, you are like the <s>Gaṅgā</s> for the enemy of <s>Tripura</s>:
when I place my head before you, you give me life merely by seizing my hair.
Talkative in conversations about you, as if with blame, delight, and concealment at once,

children.text: sa khalu sakhīnāṃ nibhṛtaṃ tvayā kṛtārthīkṛtaḥ subhagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that fortunate man has certainly been secretly made successful by you among your friends.

children.text: tvayi sarpati pathi dṛṣṭiḥ sundara vṛtivivaranirgatā tasyāḥ
children.translated_text: Handsome man, as you move along the road, her gaze, emerging through a gap in the fence,
flickers like a little fish through a net of duckweed slightly broken and trembling.

children.text: te sutanu śūnyahṛdayā ye śaṅkhaṃ śūnyahṛdayam abhidadhati
children.translated_text: Slender woman, those who call a conch empty-hearted are themselves empty-hearted,
for it has accepted a hand-saw and grasps your hand.

children.text: te śreṣṭhinaḥ kva samprati śakradhvaja yaiḥ kṛtas tavocchrāyaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Śakra</s>'s banner, where now are those guild-masters by whom your height was made?

children.text: īṣāṃ vā meḍhiṃ vādhunātanās tvāṃ vidhitsanti ||
children.translated_text: Those of the present day want to turn you into a plough-pole or a post.
When love has become thin, cut off, reddened by another's addition, and pressed together by pride,

children.text: karṇa iva kāminīnāṃ na śobhate nirbharaḥ premā ||
children.translated_text: like the ears of women, it does not shine when it is too heavy.

children.text: tasmin gatārdrabhāve vītarase śuṇṭhiśakala iva puruṣe
children.translated_text: In that man whose tenderness is gone and whose flavor is spent, like a piece of dry ginger,
even if he bears ash and is stained, the word 'urbane lover' is only a mockery.

children.text: tamasi ghane viṣame pathi jambukam ulkāmukhaṃ prapannāḥ smaḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, on a dense-dark, difficult road we have resorted to a jackal with a firebrand in its mouth.

children.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ so 'pi sakhe sthito mukhaṃ mudrayitvaiva ||
children.translated_text: What can we do? Even he stands there with his mouth shut tight.

children.text: tvām abhilaṣato mānini mama garimaguṇo 'pi doṣatāṃ yātaḥ
children.translated_text: Proud woman, because I desire you, even the virtue of my dignity has turned into a fault,

children.text: paṅkilakūlāṃ taṭinīṃ yiyāsataḥ sindhur asy eva ||
children.translated_text: like the greatness of an elephant that wants to cross a river with muddy banks.

children.text: timire'pi dūradṛśyā kaṭhināśleṣe ca rahasi mukharā ca
children.translated_text: Visible even in darkness, harsh in a close embrace, and noisy in secret,
may the row of conch bangles burst, together with the householder's head.
Beautiful woman, for your rounded form and your virtue, fit to roll on a well-adorned neck,

children.text: hārasraja iva sundari kṛtaḥ punar nāyakas taralaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a fickle lover has again been made, like a necklace-garland.
Her pride humbled by the sight, the housewife, with the surface of her cheeks brightening with joy,
covers her face with both hands, pretending to forbid kisses.
Stiffening of the body, stumbling, slackness, trembling, meditation on the beloved,

children.text: pathi pathi gaganāśleṣaḥ kāmini kas te'bhisāraguṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, at every step, embracing the sky: lover, what skill in going to a tryst is yours?
By lengthening the days, through the fierce heat of separation from you,
her life has been made scant, like that of a lotus by summer.

children.text: durjanasahavāsād api śīlotkarṣaṃ na sajjanas tyajati
children.translated_text: Even from association with bad people, a good person does not give up excellence of character;
though dwelling each fortnight in the sun, the moon, the moment it emerges, is cool.

children.text: dayitaprahitāṃ dūtīm ālambya kareṇa tamasi gacchantī
children.translated_text: Fair-limbed woman, as you go in the darkness, holding by the hand the messenger sent by your beloved,
you are visible from afar by the musk fallen from your sweat.
Your beloved's virtue has been brought to light by the fault of your own mouth.
Why are you distressed by the daily breaking and repairing of the garden fence?

children.text: dākṣiṇyān mradimānaṃ dadhataṃ mā bhānum enam avamaṃsthāḥ
children.translated_text: Do not despise this sun because, out of gentleness, he assumes softness.

children.text: raudrīm upāgate'smin kaḥ kṣamate dṛṣṭim api dātum ||
children.translated_text: When he has reached his fierce form, who is able even to cast a glance at him?
With only her star-like eye, made anxious by separation and fixed upon her beloved's face,
the breaths of the doe-eyed woman depart, wounded by the arrows of the Pulindas.
Keeping the heart set far away, hiding its secret, and extremely full of suspicion,

children.text: āśleṣo bālānāṃ bhavati khalānāṃ ca sambhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the embrace of young women, and the mingling of villains, are alike.

children.text: dvāre guravaḥ koṇe śukaḥ sakāśe śiśur gṛhe sakhyaḥ
children.translated_text: At the door are the elders, in the corner the parrot, nearby the child, and in the house the friends.
Beloved, forgive me for not enduring the time; be gracious: the day has gone by.
With pearl-ornaments of drops of curd, and charming by the offering of breasts raised by breathing,
the cowherdess embraces her beloved with limbs made languid by the labor of churning.

children.text: dalitodvegena sakhi priyeṇa lagnena rāgam āvahatā
children.translated_text: Friend, by my beloved clinging to me, removing my agitation, bringing passion,
and bewildering the bed, I have been carried away as though by betel.
Having made her beloved, though seen, seem almost unseen by revealing her breasts,

children.text: hṛdayaṃ kareṇa tāḍitam atha mithyā vyañjitatrapayā ||
children.translated_text: she struck her heart with her hand, then falsely displayed shame.
Slender woman, when your eyes, marked by the play of your brows, roll and show the rise of the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: kṣiptahale haladhara iva sarvaṃ puramarjitaṃ sutanu ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Haladhara</s> with his plough cast down, the whole city is swept away.
The bakula tree, softened by the sprinkling of mouth-wine hard to obtain and begged from a beloved,

children.text: vyathayati virahe bakulaḥ kva paricayaḥ prakṛtikaṭhinānām ||
children.translated_text: torments in separation. What acquaintance can there be with those naturally hard?

children.text: dvitrair eṣyāmi dinair iti kiṃ tad vacasi sakhi tavāśvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, what reassurance is there for you in his words, 'I shall come in two or three days'?

children.text: kathayati cirapathikaṃ taṃ dūranikhāto nakhāṅkas te ||
children.translated_text: Your nail-mark, deeply dug in from far away, declares him a long-road traveler.
Friend, when your proud talk had been stirred up by the dear one's touch, and your foot slipped because the sweat-water opened out, O mischievous-eyed one,
why do you blame those locks of his?

children.text: duṣṭagraheṇa gehini tena kuputreṇa kiṃ prajātena
children.translated_text: Housewife, what is gained by the birth of that bad son, possessed by an evil planet,
by whom his own family has been made like charcoal, just as by <s>Bhauma</s>, the planet <s>Aṅgāraka</s>?
Diamonds, showing the height of their bow-shaped brilliance, full of splendor and born from good lineage,

children.text: hīrair apsv api vīrair āpatsv api gamyate nādhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not go downward even in water; heroes too do not sink even in calamities.
Simple girl, even when <s>Smara</s> was half asleep, your glance, through its craft, took the life out of me;

children.text: mugdhe tava dṛṣṭir asāv arjunayantreṣur iva hanti ||
children.translated_text: like an arrow in <s>Arjuna</s>'s machine, it strikes.

children.text: durgatagṛhiṇī tanaye karuṇārdrā priyatame ca rāgamayī
children.translated_text: Toward her child the poor housewife is wet with compassion, and toward her beloved she is full of passion;

children.text: mugdhā ratābhiyogaṃ na manyate na pratikṣipati ||
children.translated_text: the innocent woman neither accepts nor rejects the summons to love-play.
Poor housewife, sleeping in your broken-down house, you alone greet the moon;
we, whose eyes are cheated of the moon, sport in swings among the nicula trees.
A young woman of good family, like a lamp-wick, becomes blackened precisely through cleverness;

children.text: doṣā api bhūṣāyai gaṇikāyāḥ śaśikalāyāś ca ||
children.translated_text: but faults serve as ornaments for a courtesan and for the digit of the moon.
The red rays of the sun, falling through the faces of long lattice windows,
enter the palace floor like the nails of <s>Nṛhari</s> entering the chest of the demon.

children.text: daratarale'kṣaṇi vakṣasi daronnate tava mukhe ca darahasite
children.translated_text: When your eye is a little trembling, your breast a little raised, and your face a little smiling,
let the flower be; heroic <s>Smara</s> now conquers even with only a painted bow.
This full-moon-faced woman, accompanied by wicked friends, is not for happiness now;
like the full-moon night joined with the inauspicious viṣṭi, may she become what you desire at night.

children.text: dalite palālapuñje vṛṣabhaṃ paribhavati gṛhapatau kupite
children.translated_text: When the heap of straw is broken apart and the householder angrily abuses the bull,
the ploughman's wife and her brother-in-law laugh, their faces secretly watching each other.

children.text: dīpyantāṃ ye dīptyai ghaṭitā maṇayaś ca vīrapuruṣāś ca
children.translated_text: Let gems and heroic men, formed for shining, blaze forth for brilliance;

children.text: tejaḥ svavināśāya tu nṛṇāṃ tṛṇānām iva laghūnām ||
children.translated_text: but for light men, as for blades of grass, their heat is only for their own destruction.

children.text: dhūmair aśru nipātaya daha śikhayā dahanamalinayāṅgāraiḥ
children.translated_text: Make tears fall with smoke, burn with flame, blacken with coals;

children.text: jāgarayiṣyati durgatagṛhiṇī tvāṃ tad api śiśiraniśi ||
children.translated_text: even so, in the winter night, the poor housewife will keep you awake, O fire.

children.text: dhairyaṃ nidhehi gacchatu rajanī so 'py astu sumukhi sotkaṇṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Put firmness in your heart; let the night pass, and let him too, fair-faced girl, remain longing;

children.text: praviśa hṛdi tasya dūraṃ kṣaṇadhṛtamuktā smareṣur iva ||
children.translated_text: enter deep into his heart like the arrow of <s>Smara</s>, held for a moment and then released.
At the city gate I shall see the body of the woman whose eyes are covered by curls, marked by pale nail-scars, weakened, and without full adornment,
with its tears doubled by the sight of me.
Even in undertaking <s>dharma</s>, for the wicked injury to others is the motive;
rain experiences its uselessness at the consecration of crows.
In the cold season the rivers shine with banks swollen by clefts of sandbanks, jagged from the descent of water,
as though with thick cloths from heaps of cotton.
To remove the misery of summer by resting in the shade of her own body,
alas, this charming doe practices all sorts of bodily contortions.

children.text: na hasanti jaraṭha iti yadvallavavanitā namanti nandam api
children.translated_text: The cowherd women bow even to <s>Nanda</s>, and do not laugh, saying, 'He is old';
friend, that son of <s>Yaśodā</s> is always making <s>Kandarpa</s> sprout.

children.text: nītā svabhāvam arpitavapur api vāmyaṃ na kāminī tyajati
children.translated_text: Even when brought to her true nature and even when she has given her body, a woman does not abandon contrariness;
<s>Pārvatī</s>, joined as half of <s>Hara</s>'s body, is the example there.
The weaver, unsteady with pride in his own wife's beauty, inferred from the enjoyment of city men,

children.text: nipatati padaṃ na bhūmau jñātipuras tantuvāyasya ||
children.translated_text: does not let his foot fall on the ground before his kinsmen's town.

children.text: nipatati caraṇe koṇe praviśya niśi yan nirīkṣate kas tat
children.translated_text: Who is it that, entering a corner by night, falls at your feet and looks at you?

children.text: sakhi sa khalu lokapurataḥ khalaḥ svagarimāṇam udgirati ||
children.translated_text: Friend, in front of people that very rogue proclaims his own greatness.

children.text: na vimocayituṃ śakyaḥ kṣamāṃ mahān mocito yadi kathaṃcit
children.translated_text: A great man cannot be made to give up forbearance; if somehow he is released, how could he?

children.text: mandaragirir iva garalaṃ nivartate nanu samutthāpya ||
children.translated_text: Surely, like <s>Mandara</s> mountain after churning up poison, he turns back.
It must be used with fixed steps; if one slips, it brings disaster, though another way may be possible;
who takes refuge in a bridge-plank or in a bad lord?
For elephants and good poets, whose own way of stepping delights the world,

children.text: vahatām api mahimānaṃ śobhāyai sajjanā eva ||
children.translated_text: only good people, even while bearing their greatness, are an ornament.

children.text: nottapane na snehaṃ harati na nirvāti na malino bhavati
children.translated_text: It does not take away affection when it heats, it is not extinguished, and it does not become soiled;

children.text: tasyojjvalo niśi niśi premā ratnapradīpa iva ||
children.translated_text: his bright love, night after night, is like a jewel-lamp.

children.text: nihitān nihitān ujhati niyataṃ mama pārthivān api prema
children.translated_text: Again and again my love certainly rejects even kings who are placed before it;

children.text: bhrāmaṃ bhrāmaṃ tiṣṭhati tatraiva kulālacakram iva ||
children.translated_text: wandering and wandering, it remains right there, like a potter's wheel.

children.text: nirbharam api saṃbhuktaṃ dṛṣṭyā prātaḥ piban na tṛpyāmi
children.translated_text: Though I have fully enjoyed it, drinking it with my eyes in the morning, I am not satisfied
with her unclothed hips, like a cakravāka bird with the disk of the not-cold-rayed sun.
I remember that slender woman, her pair of thighs closely joined, her fan laid upon breasts heaving with breath,
her gaze moist and angrily loving, overcome by love-play.

children.text: nirguṇa iti mṛta iti ca dvāvekārthābhidhāyinau viddhi
children.translated_text: Know that 'without virtue' and 'dead' are two expressions of one meaning;

children.text: paśya dhanurguṇaśūnyaṃ nirjīvaṃ tad iha śaṃsanti ||
children.translated_text: look, here they call a bow without a string lifeless.

children.text: nijasūkṣmasūtralambī vilocanaṃ taruṇa te kṣaṇaṃ haratu
children.translated_text: Young man, may your eye, hanging by its own fine thread, steal a moment;

children.text: ayam udgṛhītabaḍiśaḥ karkaṭa iva markaṭaḥ purataḥ ||
children.translated_text: before you is this monkey, like a crab with its hook lifted up.

children.text: nāgara gītir ivāsau grāmasthityāpi bhūṣitā sutanuḥ
children.translated_text: City-man, this slender woman, though adorned with village ways, is like a song;
musk does not become rank because it dwells in the belly of a deer.
With breasts scratched by nails, on a back made of kurabaka blossoms, your body made listless by rolling on the ground,
you steal my mind like the flower-blooded arrow that has come out after piercing the heart.

children.text: nītā laghimānam iyaṃ tasyāṃ garimāṇam adhikam arpayasi
children.translated_text: You have brought this woman to lightness, and upon that one you lay a still greater weight;

children.text: bhāra iva viṣamabhāryaḥ sudurvaho bhavati gṛhavāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a burden with an ill-matched wife, life in the house becomes very hard to bear.

children.text: na ca dūtī na ca yācñā na cāñjalir na ca kaṭākṣavikṣepaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no go-between, no entreaty, no joined palms, and no tossing of sidelong glances;
friend, for women proud of their good fortune, the first declaration is the seizing of the hair.
At night, when the two, driven by the uneven-flowered arrows, have won the taste of love through silence,
their pride itself plays on just so, the knot between husband and wife not loosened.
Taking away all the essence, even though it has been placed as if indistinguishable from her own body,

children.text: nirmokaṃ ca bhujaṅgī muñcati puruṣaṃ ca vāravadhūḥ ||
children.translated_text: a female serpent casts off her slough, and a courtesan casts off a man.
Slender woman, with difficulty you take off the bodice damp with sweat from the fatigue of dancing,
like the vine of <s>Madana</s>'s bow taking off its bark, soaked with nectar-water.

children.text: nāhaṃ vadāmi sutanu tvam aśīlā vā pracaṇḍacaritā vā
children.translated_text: Slender woman, I do not say that you are ill-conducted or fierce in your behavior;

children.text: premasvabhāvasulabhaṃ bhayam udayati mama tu hṛdayasya ||
children.translated_text: but the fear natural to love arises in my heart.
Surely you were not closely inspected by my friend, with even a third part of her eye;

children.text: hārayati yena kusumaṃ vimukhe tvayi kaṇṭha iva deve ||
children.translated_text: for when you turn away, she takes off her flower as if from the neck of a god.
With pitiless blows of nails, teeth, and fists, and with embraces of the handsome man,
passionate women, while reporting his offense, make peace.

children.text: na guṇe na lakṣaṇe'pi ca vayasi ca rūpe ca nādaro vihitaḥ
children.translated_text: No regard has been shown for merit, nor even for marks, nor for age or beauty;
O cow of good fragrance, this bell has been tied on you merely because you are <s>Kapilā</s>'s daughter.
It has causeless offense, causeless quarrel, anger, and appeasement,
and common death, life, happiness, and sorrow: marriage is victorious.

children.text: na prāpyase karābhyāṃ hṛdayān nāpaiṣi vitanuṣe bādhām
children.translated_text: You are not reached by my hands, you do not depart from my heart, and you spread pain;
you are like the tip of a flower-arrow of <s>Kusumāyudha</s>, broken off and lodged in me.

children.text: nātheti paruṣam ucitaṃ priyeti dāsety anugraho yatra
children.translated_text: Where harshly saying 'lord' is proper, and saying 'beloved' or 'slave' is a favor,

children.text: taddāmpatyam ito 'nyan nārī rajjuḥ paśuḥ puruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is marriage; anything else is a woman as rope and a man as beast.

children.text: nihitāyām asyām api saivaikā manasi me sphurati
children.translated_text: Even though this one has been placed near me, that one alone flashes in my mind,
like a row of letters on a leaf when another line has been laid over it, beloved.
As if a vine had been placed as a sign above the spot where treasure is buried,

children.text: lobhayati tava tanūdari jaghanataṭād upari romālī ||
children.translated_text: slender-waisted woman, the row of hair above your hip-bank entices me.
When she has half-closed her eyes, you steal her heart all the way to its end;

children.text: na subhaga samucitam īdṛśam aṅgulidāne bhujaṃ girasi ||
children.translated_text: handsome man, this is not fitting: when given a finger, you swallow the arm.

children.text: nītvāgāraṃ rajanījāgaram ekaṃ ca sādaraṃ dattvā
children.translated_text: After bringing you home and respectfully granting you one night of wakefulness,

children.text: acireṇa kair na taruṇair durgāpattrīva muktāsi ||
children.translated_text: by what young men were you not soon abandoned like a leaf used for <s>Durgā</s>?

children.text: nakṣatre'gnāv indāv udare kanake maṇau dṛśi samudre
children.translated_text: Whatever brilliance is in the stars, in fire, in the moon, in the belly, in gold, in jewels, in the eye, and in the ocean,

children.text: yat khalu tejas tad akhilam ojāyitam abjamitrasya ||
children.translated_text: all of it has become the splendor of the friend of the lotus.

children.text: na savarṇo na ca rūpaṃ na saṃskriyā kāpi naiva sā prakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: There is no sameness of color, no beauty, no refinement at all, and that nature is gone;
in the calamity of separation from you, the girl has become like Apabhraṃśa speech.

children.text: na vibhūṣaṇe tavāsthā vapurguṇenaiva jayasi sakhi yūnaḥ
children.translated_text: You have no concern for ornaments; by the quality of your body alone, friend, you conquer young men,
like <s>Kusumeṣu</s>'s wrestling art, despising missiles and weapons.

children.text: netrākṛṣṭo bhrāmaṃ bhrāmaṃ preyān yathā yathāsti tathā
children.translated_text: As the beloved, drawn by the eyes, wanders round and round in whatever way he is,

children.text: sakhi manthayati mano mama dadhibhāṇḍaṃ manthadaṇḍa iva ||
children.translated_text: friend, he churns my mind like a churning-stick in a curd-pot.
Fashioning you, slender woman, in many colors and forms as something charming,
she imagines you on every wall like a painter's brush.

children.text: pathikāsaktā kiṃcin na veda ghanakalam agopitā gopī
children.translated_text: The cowherdess, a little attached to the traveler, does not know the deep, sweet sound, and she is not hidden;
O row of parrots, you depart in vain with your cries of playful art.

children.text: praṇamati paśyati cumbati saṃśliṣyati pulakamukulitair aṅgaiḥ
children.translated_text: The woman in separation bows to, looks at, kisses, and embraces with limbs budding with gooseflesh
her left arm, throbbing for union with her beloved.

children.text: praviśasi na ca nirgantuṃ jānāsi vyākulatvam ātanuṣe
children.translated_text: You enter, but you do not know how to come out, and you produce bewilderment;
boy, in her mind you are like <s>Abhimanyu</s> in the wheel-formation.
Look: the mango-crest, noisy with a bee, is well matched,

children.text: api ca picumandamukule maukulikulam ākulaṃ milati ||
children.translated_text: and even on the neem bud the confused swarm of bees gathers.
Fair-faced man, why do you uselessly wish to take the mirror, whose face is filled by reflection,
from my friend's hand, through delusion that it is a play-lotus?
Just as the moon, from the summit of the eastern mountain, dwells in the middle of the sky,

children.text: tvāṃ sakhi paśyāmi tathā chāyām iva saṃkucanmānām ||
children.translated_text: so, friend, I see you like a shadow, your pride shrinking.

children.text: prāṅgaṇakoṇe'pi niśāpatiḥ sa tāpaṃ sudhāmayo harati
children.translated_text: Even in the corner of the courtyard, that moon, made of nectar, removes heat;

children.text: yadi māṃ rajanijvara iva sakhi sa na niruṇaddhi gehapatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: friend, if only the householder, like a night-fever, did not restrain me.
She whose body is distressed by her husband's horripilation, and who is afraid even at the sight of her own shadow,

children.text: abhisarati subhaga sā tvāṃ vidalantī kaṇṭakaṃ tamasi ||
children.translated_text: handsome man, comes to meet you in the dark, splitting thorns as she goes.

children.text: pratibhūḥ śuko vipakṣe daṇḍaḥ śṛṅgārasaṃkathā guruṣu
children.translated_text: A parrot is the surety for the opposing side; punishment is talk of love before the elders;
the stake is acting like a man. Girl, consider what the inheritance is.

children.text: paramohanāya mukto niṣkaruṇe taruṇi tava kaṭākṣo 'yam
children.translated_text: Pitiless young woman, this sidelong glance of yours, released for supreme bewilderment,

children.text: viśikha iva kalitakarṇaḥ praviśati hṛdayaṃ na niḥsarati ||
children.translated_text: enters the heart like an arrow fitted to the ear, and does not come out.
With her feet touching the ground, kissing, her eyes sweet with love and fear,
the slender woman, with her chin set on the top of the wall, did not fall.

children.text: prātar upāgatya mṛṣā vadataḥ sakhi nāsya vidyate vrīḍā
children.translated_text: Friend, he has no shame when he comes in the morning and speaks falsely,
this man who is not ashamed even by the burnt lampblack clinging to his face.
Look, slender-waisted woman: the northern one, having reached <s>Phālguna</s>, has defeated his rival.

children.text: vairāṭir iva pataṅgaḥ pratyānayanaṃ karoti gavām ||
children.translated_text: like the moth born from <s>Virāṭa</s>, brings the cows back.

children.text: pramadavanaṃ tava ca stanaśailaṃ mūlaṃ gabhīrasarasāṃ ca
children.translated_text: Your pleasure-garden, your mountain-like breasts, and the source of deep lakes:
the coolness banished by summer from the world takes refuge in this hard-to-reach triad.

children.text: proñchati tavāparādhaṃ mānaṃ mardayati nirvṛtiṃ harati
children.translated_text: Handsome man, the long wakeful night wipes away your offense, crushes pride, steals contentment,

children.text: svakṛtān nihanti śapathāñ jāgaradīrghā niśā subhaga ||
children.translated_text: and destroys the oaths made by yourself.

children.text: priya āyāte dūrād abhūta iva saṅgamo 'bhavat pūrvaḥ
