children.translated_text: When the beloved had come from afar, the first union became as though it had never happened;
pride, weeping, and reconciliation came again at the beginning of the next lovemaking nearby.
On the peak of the eastern mountain, darkness, touched by the rays of the approaching sun,
appears like the bloodied body of <s>Andhaka</s> impaled on a spear.
O languid-eyed woman, with navel turned aside, the three belly-folds vanished, and the tips of the dark breasts exposed,
the body, with the white line of the hips much displayed, cannot endure the man's position.
Tender-limbed woman, just beginning lovemaking, why do you bear drops of sweat?
It is as if spring, bent down, were setting the bowstring on the flower-arrowed god's bow-creeper.

children.text: puṃsāṃ darśaya sundari mukhendum īṣat trpām apākṛtya
children.translated_text: Beautiful woman, show men the moon of your face, casting off a little shame,

children.text: jāyājita iti rūḍhā janaśrutir me yaśo bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: so that the established rumor, 'he has been conquered by his wife,' may become my fame.

children.text: prasaratu śarattriyāmā jaganti dhavalayatu dhāma tuhināṃśoḥ
children.translated_text: Let the autumn night spread; let the radiance of the moon whiten the worlds.
For female cakora birds in cages, even a particle-like portion makes no difference.
She has come for the first time, full of longing; if there is fault because you have been long delayed,

children.text: vakṣyanti sāṅgarāgāḥ pathi taravas tava samādhānam ||
children.translated_text: the trees along the road, red with aṅgāra, will give your explanation.
My mind remembers her when her garment had fallen, her hand placed on her breast, her thighs hidden by her dense hips,
and the lamp shaken by hundreds of puffing breaths broken by teeth-marks.
On the mountain, surrounded by masses of flashing jewels that are great herbs, as on a couch of play,

children.text: kāñcīguṇa iva patitaḥ sthitaikaratnaḥ phaṇī sphurati ||
children.translated_text: a serpent shines, fallen like a girdle-cord, with a single gem remaining fixed.
Cloud, in the rainy season you roam through the quarters, carrying the slopes of mountain ranges.

children.text: capalāntara ghana kiṃ tava vacanīyaṃ pavanavaśyo 'si ||
children.translated_text: Fickle within, what can be said of you? You are subject to the wind.
This hem of your garment, pulled excessively by your hand, grows thinner day by day.

children.text: nijanāyakam atikṛpaṇaṃ kathayati kugrāma iva viralaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sparse like a wretched village, it tells of its own most pitiful master.
Traveler, how do you endure the unbearable mass of restless, flashing drops of rain-cloud water,
like molten gold from <s>Mayapura</s>, heated by the fire of <s>Śiva</s>'s arrow?

children.text: pathikaṃ śrameṇa suptaṃ darataralā taruṇi sumadhuracchāyā
children.translated_text: Young woman, as the traveler sleeps from weariness, you, slightly trembling and of very sweet shade,
with your braid hanging down, comfort him like a branch bearing a creeper.
She, whose full high hips and thighs do not grant other women even entry,

children.text: yā luptakīlabhāvaṃ yātā hṛdi bahir adṛśyāsi ||
children.translated_text: has gone into your heart, with the latch removed, invisible outside.

children.text: prātar nidrāti yathā yathātmajā lulitaniḥsahair aṅgaiḥ
children.translated_text: In the morning, as and as the daughter sleeps with limbs rumpled and powerless,

children.text: jāmātari muditamanās tathā tathā sādarā śvaśrūḥ ||
children.translated_text: so and so the mother-in-law, delighted in her son-in-law, becomes more respectful.
Though moved by love, my beloved was stopped by my feigned angry sidelong glances,
then, trembling with fear, was seized by the neck with laughing eagerness.

children.text: priyadurnayena hṛdaya sphuṭasi yadi sphuṭanam api tava ślāghyam
children.translated_text: Heart, if you burst because of the beloved's misconduct, even your bursting is praiseworthy,
like that of the hem of the garment made into a couch for his battle of love.
The bee, greedy for a lotus pond full of water far away by the fragrance brought on the wind,
without first testing his own wings, is going, alas, to disaster.
With the burden of <s>Keśava</s>'s breast made light by love, and with her jar-like breasts broad with great horripilation,
the innocent young woman secretly laughs at the heaviness of <s>Govardhana</s> mountain.
The doe-eyed woman's life-breaths, helpless in separation from her beloved,
are guarded even by co-wives, natural enemies, because they fear the breaking up of the household.

children.text: prakaṭayasi rāgam adhikaṃ lapanam idaṃ vakrimāṇam āvahati
children.translated_text: Messenger, this speech of yours reveals excessive passion and assumes crookedness,

children.text: prīṇayati ca pratipadaṃ dūti śukasyeva dayitasya ||
children.translated_text: yet at every word it delights the beloved, like the speech of a parrot.
For the young girl entering her beloved's heart, occupied by strong youth,
the path is made by the sword of her eyes, newly whetted and slightly trembling.
When love has grown firm through offense in affection, anger, reconciliation, trust, play, and skill,
how can it be carried away by a young girl's mere curiosity?

children.text: pūrvair eva caritair jarato 'pi pūjyatā bhavataḥ
children.translated_text: Even though you are old, your honor exists because of former deeds alone.

children.text: muñca madam asya gandhād yuvabhir gaja gaūjanīyo 'si ||
children.translated_text: Give up pride in its scent, elephant; because of young men you are fit to be despised by cows.

children.text: prathamaṃ praveśitā yā vāsāgāraṃ kathañcana sakhībhiḥ
children.translated_text: She who was somehow first led into the bedchamber by her friends

children.text: na śṛṇotīva prātaḥ sā nirgamanasya saṅketam ||
children.translated_text: in the morning seems not to hear the signal for departure.

children.text: pūjā vinā pratiṣṭhāṃ nāsti na mantraṃ vinā pratiṣṭhā ca
children.translated_text: There is no consecration without worship, and no consecration without mantra.
Let the one who rejects both of these behold a divine stone.
Greater than before are the wife's honor, love, joking affection, and trust;

children.text: bhīr adhikeyaṃ kathayati rāgaṃ bālāvibhaktam iva ||
children.translated_text: this increased fear declares passion, as if not yet divided by a young girl.
The serpent serving as <s>Śambhu</s>'s sacred thread, knowing the pain of embracing the hard, full, horripilated jar-like breasts,
desires that the goddess should take offense in pride.

children.text: priya āyāto dūrād iti yā prītir babhūva gehinyāḥ
children.translated_text: The joy that arose in the housewife because 'my beloved has come from afar'

children.text: pathikebhyaḥ pūrvāgata iti garvāt sāpi śataśikharā ||
children.translated_text: became a hundred-peaked thing through pride, because he had arrived before the travelers.

children.text: pṛṣṭhaṃ prayaccha mā spṛśa dūrād apasarpa vihitavaimukhya
children.translated_text: Turn your back, do not touch me, go away from afar, O one who has turned your face away.

children.text: tvām anudhāvati taraṇis tad api guṇākarṣataraleyam ||
children.translated_text: The sun runs after you; even so, this one, trembling because drawn by your virtues, follows.
The garment sent by my beloved, marked by the joining of both hands yellow-red with saffron,
teaches me to make a thousand petitioning gestures with folded hands.
When the eastern horizon has hidden her, night places its lower lip on the face of its beloved,
as if, concealed by the eastern mountain, it were placing the twilight-redness on the face of day.
Faithless one, drained dry by another man's pitiless wanton wife, you are not to be led away with anger.
Burned by affection and scorched within, I weep when I see your thinness.

children.text: prāṅgaṇa eva kadā māṃ śliṣyantī manykampikucakalaśā
children.translated_text: When will she, embracing me right in the courtyard, her jar-like breasts trembling with passion,

children.text: aṃsaniṣaṇṇamukhī sā snapayati bāṣpeṇa mama pṛṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: with her face resting on my shoulder, bathe my back with tears?

children.text: pretaiḥ praśastasattvā sāśru vṛkair vīkṣitā skhaladgrāsaiḥ
children.translated_text: Praised by ghosts for her courage, watched tearfully by wolves whose morsels slip from their mouths,
the young woman kisses the face of the dead man, while corpse-mouth firebrands look on.

children.text: piśunaḥ khalu sujanānāṃ khalam eva puro vidhāya jetavyaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely a slanderer of good people must be conquered only by placing a villain before him.

children.text: kṛtvā jvaram ātmīyaṃ jigāya bāṇaṃ raṇe viṣṇuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By making his own fever, <s>Viṣṇu</s> conquered <s>Bāṇa</s> in battle.

children.text: piba madhupa bakulakalikāṃ dūre rasanāgramātram ādhāya
children.translated_text: Drink the bakula bud, bee, placing only the tip of your tongue from afar.
When the honey ends with the lip-paint, you uselessly offer your whole mouth.

children.text: prāyeṇaiva hi malinā malinānām āśrayatvam upayānti
children.translated_text: For the most part, the stained become the refuge of the stained.
The cleaving of <s>Kālindī</s>'s bank becomes the breaking open of <s>Kāliya</s>'s hood.
See: out of fear that her beloved's body might be broken apart, clinging to the body of the moon-crested god,
lovely <s>Umā</s>, whose only deity is her beloved, bears <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> on her head.
In regions watered by rivers of tears from travelers' wives' eyes,
the mass of clouds seems to have been coiled by fate with <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>'s bow.
Although the householder had come home with difficulty from afar, among neighbors, friends, and relatives,
his wife, excessively eager for play, hid him away for one day.

children.text: parapaṭa iva rajakībhir malino bhuktvāpi nirdayaṃ tābhiḥ
children.translated_text: Base man, though you have been enjoyed mercilessly by those wanton women, like another's cloth by washerwomen, and made soiled,
you have been released by the wantons without even the taking of payment.
When her beloved, his head red with lac from many women, is mocked by his friend,
the shame fashioned at that very moment betrays her good fortune among her companions.
Her heart, freed from attachment to that mass of hair which deserved binding,
seems split open under the pretext of the red-sindur part in her hair.

children.text: balam api vasati mayīti śreṣṭhini gurugarvagadgadaṃ vadati
children.translated_text: When the guild-master says, with his voice choked by heavy pride, 'Power too resides in me,'
his wife looked at the people's faces with a smile concealed.
A bee, carried by a strong breeze and filled with the fragrance of freshly opened lotuses,
is drawn by the lotus-bed as if by a fishing-line with a hook cast into its nose.

children.text: bāṇaṃ harir iva kurute sujano bahudoṣam apy adoṣam iva
children.translated_text: Like <s>Hari</s> with <s>Bāṇa</s>, a good man makes even one with many faults seem faultless.

children.text: yāvad doṣaṃ jāgrati malimlucā iva punaḥ piśunāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But slanderers, like night-thieves, remain awake so long as there is a fault.

children.text: bauddhasyeva kṣaṇiko yadyapi bahuvallabhasya tava bhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Though your feeling, since you have many beloveds, is momentary like that of a Buddhist,

children.text: bhagnā bhagnā bhrūr iva na tu tasyā vighaṭate maitrī ||
children.translated_text: her friendship does not break apart, though it is broken again and again like her eyebrow.

children.text: bāṣpākulaṃ pralapator gṛhiṇi nivartasva kānta gaccheti
children.translated_text: As they babbled with tears in their eyes, 'Housewife, turn back,' and 'Beloved, go on,'
the day of the couple passed on the lake-shore up to the limit of following along.
Thinking first of the charms and bonds of a young girl, though unable to master them in his heart,
I grieve for that housewife herself, deprived of honor.

children.text: bhramasi prakaṭayasi radaṃ karaṃ prasārayasi tṛṇam api śrayasi
children.translated_text: You wander, you bare your tusk, you stretch out your trunk, you even resort to grass.

children.text: dhiṅ mānaṃ tava kuñjara jīvaṃ na juhoṣi jaṭharāgnau ||
children.translated_text: Shame on your pride, elephant, that you do not sacrifice your life in the fire of your belly.

children.text: bhūtimayaṃ kurute'gnis tṛṇam api saṃlagnam enam api bhajataḥ
children.translated_text: Fire turns even straw that has come into contact with it into ash-like splendor; and for one who serves this man too,
I suspect that that same golden state of yours is blocked by heaviness.

children.text: bhavati nidāghe dīrghe yatheha yamuneva yāminī tanvī
children.translated_text: Just as here, in the long summer, the night becomes slender like the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: dvīpā iva divasā api tathā krameṇa prathīyāṃsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too the days, like islands, gradually become broader.
Traveler, set by you in the great fire of affection, the slender woman is like a lump of gold.

children.text: tanvī hastenāpi spraṣṭum aśuddhair na sā śakyā ||
children.translated_text: She cannot be touched even by a hand that is impure.
With one earring fallen to the ground and a reed-leaf set as an ornament, this innocent girl,
as she watches, drives away even the mass of dust raised by passion with her sighs.

children.text: bhavatāliṅgi bhujaṃgī jātaḥ kila bhogicakravartī tvam
children.translated_text: Since a female serpent has been embraced by you, you have supposedly become an emperor of serpents.

children.text: kañcuka vanecarīstanam abhilaṣataḥ sphurati laghimā te ||
children.translated_text: But armor, as you desire the breast of a forest woman, your lightness becomes apparent.
Praised by the beautiful-eyed wife of the village chief as one who lives on alms,

children.text: rakṣaka jayasi yad ekaḥ śūnye surasadasi sukham asmi ||
children.translated_text: guardian, you triumph, since I am happy alone in the empty temple of the gods.
When an old man, unable to enjoy pleasures, guards them with mere glances, and is turned away,

children.text: vṛddhasya pramadāpi śrīr api bhṛtyasya bhogāya ||
children.translated_text: both the woman and fortune itself become objects of enjoyment for his servant.

children.text: bhavitāsi rajani yasyām adhvaśramaśāntaye padaṃ dadhatīm
children.translated_text: Night, you will be the one in which, when I set down my foot to soothe the fatigue of the road,

children.text: sa balād valayitajaṅghābaddhāṃ mām urasi pātayati ||
children.translated_text: he will forcibly cast me on his chest, caught with my thighs encircled.
Friend, for refined gold that has become fit to be an ornament after being purified by testing,

children.text: puruṣasya ca kanakasya ca yukto garimā sarāgasya ||
children.translated_text: and for a man too, weight joined with passion is proper.

children.text: bhasmapuruṣe'pi giriśe snehamayī tvam ucitena subhagāsi
children.translated_text: Even toward <s>Giriśa</s>, a man of ash, you are full of affection; lovely woman, this is fitting.
The people's saying about you is false, that you are the daughter of the mountain of herbs.
Love-awake, in sleep, moist with affection, he sees the girl's plump pair of thighs hidden by fear,
sighing and sighing.

children.text: bhramarīva koṣagarbhe gandhahṛtā kusumam anusarantī tvām
children.translated_text: Like a female bee inside a bud, carried off by fragrance and following the flower,

children.text: avyaktaṃ kūjantī saṅketaṃ tamasi sā bhramati ||
children.translated_text: she wanders in the darkness toward that tryst, humming indistinctly after you.

children.text: bhrāmaṃ bhrāmaṃ sthitayā snehe tava payasi tatra tatraiva
children.translated_text: Having circled and circled, remaining in your water of affection at the very same places,
she has behaved like a boat fallen into whirlpools, casting modesty aside.
Virtuous woman, you twist the cord near the courtyard of your own house, fit to be seized by the neck...
O ploughman's daughter, you bind young bulls as if with the rope of a stake.
There is fire in your forehead-eye, the moon on your crest, and jewel-lamps of serpents on your body;

children.text: tad api tamomaya eva tvam īśa kaḥ prakṛtim atiśete ||
children.translated_text: even so, O <s>Isa</s>, you are made of darkness alone. Who surpasses his own nature?

children.text: madhumadavītavrīḍā yathā yathā lapati saṃmukhaṃ bālā
children.translated_text: As, freed from shame by the intoxication of spring, the young girl chatters face to face,

children.text: tanmukham ajātatṛptis tathā tathā vallabhaḥ pibati ||
children.translated_text: so and so her beloved, not yet satisfied, drinks in her face.

children.text: mitrair ālocya samaṃ guru kṛtvā kadanam api samārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having consulted together with friends and made even distress a serious thing, it was begun;

children.text: arthaḥ satām iva hato mukhavailakṣyeṇa māno 'yam ||
children.translated_text: like the wealth of good men, this pride was destroyed by embarrassment of the face.

children.text: mama rāgiṇo manasvini karam arpayato dadāsi pṛṣṭham api
children.translated_text: Proud lady, when I, passionate, offer my hand, you give me even your back;

children.text: yadi tad api kamalabandhor iva manye svasya saubhāgyam ||
children.translated_text: if so, I regard even that as my own good fortune, like the lotus-kinsman, the sun.

children.text: mā spṛśa mām iti sakupitam iva bhaṇitaṃ vyañjitā na ca vrīḍā
children.translated_text: 'Do not touch me,' she said as if angry, yet no shame was revealed;
when embraced, she let out with a smile, 'Improper man, what are you doing?'

children.text: mūlāni ca niculānāṃ hṛdayāni ca kūlavasatikulaṭānām
children.translated_text: The roots of the niculā trees and the hearts of wanton women dwelling on your banks,
O <s>Godavari</s>, drunk and maddened by clouds, why do you tear them apart?
Even the excellence of virtues in the steadfast, like the heartwood of Malaya trees,
when fallen upon a dull time, serves only for neglect, not for merit.

children.text: madhumathanamaulimāle sakhi tulayasi tulasi kiṃ mudhā rādhām
children.translated_text: Friend <s>Tulasi</s>, garland on the head of <s>Madhumathana</s>, why vainly compare yourself with <s>Radha</s>?

children.text: yat tava padam adasīyaṃ surabhayituṃ saurabhodbhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For your outburst of fragrance exists to perfume her feet.
When, after counting the appointed days, my beloved will go to me with kisses and embraces,
that night, unable for love-play for so long, was mourned by her in advance.

children.text: mṛgamadanidānam aṭavī kuṅkumam api kṛṣakavāṭikā vahati
children.translated_text: The forest bears the source of musk; even the farmer's garden bears saffron;
but, O courtesan of the marketplace, you alone are the whole wealth of the city.

children.text: madhudivaseṣu bhrāmyan yathā viśati mānasaṃ bhramaraḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, as in the spring days a bee wandering about enters the mānasa lotus-lake,
so too does the arrow of <s>Madana</s>, resembling an iron thorn, enter the mind.

children.text: mayi calite tava muktā dṛśaḥ svabhāvāt priye sapānīyāḥ
children.translated_text: Beloved, when I set out, your pearl-like glances, naturally full of water,

children.text: satyam amūlyāḥ sadyaḥ prayānti mama hṛdayahāratvam ||
children.translated_text: truly priceless, at once become necklaces that steal my heart.

children.text: mugdhe mama manasi śarāḥ smarasya pañcāpi santataṃ lagnāḥ
children.translated_text: Innocent girl, all five arrows of <s>Smara</s> are constantly fixed in my mind;

children.text: śaṅke stanaguṭikādvayam arpitam etena tava hṛdaye ||
children.translated_text: I suspect that by this he has placed the pair of pellets, your breasts, in your heart.
The melodies that follow the holes of the flute set to the mouth of <s>Madhumathana</s>

children.text: hanta haranti mano mama nalikāviśikhāḥ smarasyeva ||
children.translated_text: alas, steal my mind like the reed-arrows of <s>Smara</s>.
Friend, between two great, well-rounded, high things, fit to seize the heart,

children.text: sajjanayoḥ stanayor iva nirantaraṃ saṃgataṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: there is always close union, as between good people, or between breasts.

children.text: mama vāritasya bahubhir bhūyo bhūyaḥ svayaṃ ca bhāvayataḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, though many have restrained me, and though I myself have reflected again and again,

children.text: jāto diśīva tasyāṃ sakhe na vinivartate mohaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my delusion, born in that direction as it were, does not turn back.
Tree, you are sunk in the current of the <s>Narmada</s>, carried away by the sidelong glances of her waves;

children.text: yady ucyase taruvara bhraṣṭo bhraṃśo 'pi te ślāghyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if you are called fallen, even your fall is praiseworthy.

children.text: menām ullāsayati smerayati hariṃ giriṃ ca vimukhayati
children.translated_text: It delights <s>Mena</s>, makes <s>Hari</s> smile, and turns the mountain away;
at the wedding, <s>Girisa</s>'s trembling hand delays the ritual hand-clasp.
When shall I drink the nectar of her lower lip, her face fragrant with wine, its tilaka damp with sweat, her words stumbling, her reddish eyes rolling,
after pushing her face aside?

children.text: medinyāṃ tava nipatati na padaṃ bahuvallabheti garveṇa
children.translated_text: Your foot does not fall on the ground because of pride that you have many lovers;

children.text: āśliṣya kair na taruṇais turīva vasanair vimuktāsi ||
children.translated_text: yet, like cotton freed from its coverings, by what young men have you not been embraced?

children.text: mūle nisargamadhuraṃ samarpayanto rasaṃ puro virasāḥ
children.translated_text: Naturally sweet at the root, offering juice, but tasteless in front,

children.text: ikṣava iva parapuruṣā vividheṣu raseṣu vinidheyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: other men, like sugarcanes, are to be assigned to different tastes.

children.text: mahati snehe nihitaḥ kusumaṃ bahu dattam arcito bahuśaḥ
children.translated_text: Placed in great affection, given many flowers, and worshipped often,

children.text: vakras tad api śanaiścara iva sakhi duṣṭagraho dayitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet crooked, like <s>Sanaiścara</s>, friend, the beloved is a malignant planet.

children.text: mā śabarataruṇi pīvaravakṣoruhayor bhareṇa bhaja garvam
children.translated_text: Do not, young Śabara woman, be proud of the weight of your swelling breasts;

children.text: nirmokair api śobhā yayor bhujaṅgībhir unmuktaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: they have beauty even from the cast-off sloughs abandoned by female serpents.

children.text: mama kupitāyāś chāyāṃ bhūmāv āliṅgya sakhi milatpulakaḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, when I am angry, he embraces my shadow on the ground, with horripilation arising;

children.text: snehamayatvam anujjhan karoti kiṃ naiṣa mām aruṣam ||
children.translated_text: not giving up his nature full of affection, does he not make me free of anger?

children.text: muṣita iva kṣaṇavirahe ripur iva kusumeṣukelisaṅgrāme
children.translated_text: As if robbed in a moment's separation, as if an enemy in the battle of <s>Kusumesu</s>'s play,

children.text: dāsa iva śramasamaye bhajan natāṅgīṃ na tṛpyāmi ||
children.translated_text: as if a servant at the time of fatigue, I am not satisfied while attending on the slender-limbed woman.
Why do you abandon the proud woman, thinking that the force of anger is doubled by resolve?

children.text: snehabhavaḥ payasāgniḥ sāntvena ca roṣa unmiṣati ||
children.translated_text: Fire born of affection flares up with water, and anger with conciliation.

children.text: malayajam apasārya ghanaṃ vījanavighnaṃ vidhāya bāhubhyām
children.translated_text: Pushing away the thick sandal paste and making the arms an obstacle to the fan,
the couple, heedless of summer because of the fever of <s>Smara</s>, embrace.

children.text: mahato 'pi hi viśvāsān mahāśayā dadhati nālpam api laghavaḥ
children.translated_text: For from a great trust, the great-hearted hold even a small thing; the small do not hold even a little from great trust.
The ocean contains mountains, but summer rivers do not contain even a frog.

children.text: madhudhāreva na muñcasi mānini rūkṣāpi mādhurīṃ sahajām
children.translated_text: Proud lady, like a stream of honey, even when harsh you do not abandon your innate sweetness;

children.text: kṛtamukhabhaṅgāpi rasaṃ dadāsi mama sarid ivāmbhodheḥ ||
children.translated_text: though your face is made crooked, you give me delight, like a river to the ocean.
Housewife, by the sounds of the lute-strings, as if by blows from bowstrings drawn by <s>Madana</s>,
whose mind among young travelers does not tremble?

children.text: mama bhayam asyāḥ kopo nirvedo 'syā mamāpi mandākṣam
children.translated_text: My fear, her anger, her weariness, and my own bashfulness:
where did all this vanish into the air, when our necks were bent to hide our smiles?

children.text: muktāmbaraiva dhāvatu nipatatu sahasā trimārgagā vāstu
children.translated_text: Let the <s>Trimargaga</s> run with her garment loosed, or let her suddenly fall, or let her be;
this <s>Narmada</s> alone has a current suited to the origin of my lineage.

children.text: mṛgamadalepanam enaṃ nīlanicolaiva niśi niṣeva tvam
children.translated_text: Serve this musk-anointed man at night, clad only in a dark-blue cloak.
Friend, in the <s>Kalindi</s> she is like a beautiful bee-woman on a blue lotus.

children.text: mama sakhyā nayanapathe militaḥ śakto na kaścid api calitum
children.translated_text: When my friend had come into the path of his eyes, no one at all was able to move.
Traveler, you have fallen into a dangerous place: this is the toll-house of <s>Kusumaketu</s>, the flower-bannered god of love.

children.text: mahatā priyeṇa nirmitam apriyam api subhaga sahyatāṃ yāti
children.translated_text: Fair one, even something unpleasant, when done by a greatly beloved person, becomes bearable.
The loss of youth through the birth of a son is certainly no cause for grief.

children.text: mānagrahagurukopād anu dayitāty eva rocate mahyam
children.translated_text: Because of the beloved woman's heavy anger, seized by pride, she pleases me all the more,
like a golden ornament whose pure nature has been marked by burning.
Avoiding young men, thorny bushes that catch at the hem of her garment,

children.text: vana iva pure'pi vicarati puruṣaṃ tvām eva jānantī ||
children.translated_text: she wanders in the city as if in a forest, knowing you alone as a man.
We have come to you, learned ones, with skill in words alone.

children.text: antarbhavati bhavatsv api nābhaktas tan na vijñātam ||
children.translated_text: That there can be one without devotion even among you is something we did not know.

children.text: yatra na dūtī yatra snigdhā na dṛśo 'pi nipuṇayā nihitāḥ
children.translated_text: Where there was no messenger, where not even affectionate glances were placed by a clever woman,
where there were not yet words, that feeling has been made manifest by love.

children.text: yā nīyate sapatny praviśya yāvarjitā bhujaṅgena
children.translated_text: She who is led in among co-wives, and who, on entering, is rejected by the serpent-like lover,

children.text: yamunāyā iva tasyāḥ sakhi malinaṃ jīvanaṃ manye ||
children.translated_text: friend, I think her life is dark, like that of the <s>Yamuna</s>.

children.text: yasminnayaśo 'pi yaśo hrīr vighno māna eva dauḥśīlyam
children.translated_text: In him even disgrace is glory, shame is an obstacle, pride itself is bad conduct,

children.text: laghutā guṇajñatā kiṃ navo yuvā sakhi na te dṛṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and lightness is appreciation of merit. Friend, have you not seen this new young man?

children.text: yad vīkṣyate khalānāṃ māhātmyaṃ kvāpi daivayogena
children.translated_text: When, by some turn of fate, the greatness of the wicked is seen anywhere,

children.text: kākānām iva śauklyaṃ tad api hi na cirād anarthāya ||
children.translated_text: like whiteness in crows, even that before long becomes a source of harm.

children.text: yat khalu khalamukhahutavahavinihitam api śuddhim eva parameti
children.translated_text: What, even when placed in the fire of a wicked person's mouth, reaches supreme purity,

children.text: tad analaśaucam ivāṃśukam iha loke durlabhaṃ prema ||
children.translated_text: that love is hard to find in this world, like a cloth purified by fire.

children.text: yan nāvadhim arthayate pātheyārthaṃ dadāti sarvasvam
children.translated_text: Because he does not ask about the end of the journey and gives all his wealth for provisions,
by that man a most terrible suspicion has been laid upon this woman's heart.
Young woman, by your wheel-bright hips, spreading jealousy and hostility among young men,
the whole village has been disturbed, as if by a scoundrel.
May this union of you two, whose minds are alike and whose difference is utterly absent for as long as life lasts,

children.text: nadayor ivaiṣa yuvayoḥ saṅgo rasam adhikam āvahatu ||
children.translated_text: bring an ever greater sweetness, like the meeting of two rivers.

children.text: yan nihitāṃ śekharayasi mālāṃ sā yātu śaṭha bhavantam iti
children.translated_text: 'Let the garland that you have set on your head go to you, cheat!'

children.text: praharantīṃ śirasi padā smarāmi tāṃ garvagurukopām ||
children.translated_text: I remember her, heavy with proud anger, striking me on the head with her foot.

children.text: yauvanaguptiṃ patyau bandhuṣu mugdhatvam ārjavaṃ guruṣu
children.translated_text: Keeping her youth hidden before her husband, innocence before her relatives, and straightforwardness before her elders,
the ploughman's wife is praised by young men only by implication.

children.text: yo na gurubhir na mitrair na vivekenāpi naiva ripuhasitaiḥ
children.translated_text: He who had not previously been restrained by elders, by friends, by discernment, or even by enemies' laughter,

children.text: niyamitapūrvaḥ sundari sa vinītatvaṃ tvayā nītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: beautiful woman, has been brought by you to discipline.

children.text: yanmūlam ārdram udakaiḥ kusumaṃ pratiparva phalabharaḥ paritaḥ
children.translated_text: Your root is wet with water, flowers appear at every joint, and all around there is a burden of fruit.
Tree, therefore you grow intoxicated, without considering what comes from association with waves.
Let him bear pride in his qualities, on whose lap the friend sleeps with folded hands, resting after love's battle,
like a creeper of love's bow lying on a fine cloth.
If female elephants live even on a saptacchada tree merely from the scent of ichor,

children.text: kim iti madapaṅkamalināṃ karī kapolasthalīṃ vahati ||
children.translated_text: why does the elephant bear his cheek-region stained with the mud of rut?
Since the row of hemp plants has merely grown higher and opened clusters of flowers,
from that time the village chief's daughter has become fond of yellow garments.

children.text: yamunātaraṅgataralaṃ na kuvalayaṃ kusumalāvi tava sulabham
children.translated_text: Flower-gatherer, the blue lotus trembling in the waves of the <s>Yamuna</s> is not easy for you to obtain,

children.text: yadi saurabhānusārī jhaṅkārī bhramati na bhramaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: if the humming bee, following its fragrance, does not wander there.
In tales of <s>Krishna</s>, whose head was washed with the water of royal consecration,
<s>Radha</s>, her eyes slow with the weight of pride, looks at his lotus feet.
Where the householder rejoices as he pulls the hair with his hand of his beloved angered in a quarrel of love,

children.text: bhavati bhavanaṃ tad anyat prāgvaṃśaḥ parṇaśālā vā ||
children.translated_text: that is truly a home; the rest is an ancestral hall or a leaf-hut.

children.text: rogo rājāyata iti janavādaṃ satyam adya kalayāmi
children.translated_text: Today, fair one, I recognize as true the popular saying that illness becomes a king,
since, after my former health, you have come to the edge of my bed.

children.text: ruddhasvarasaprasarasyālibhir agre nataṃ priyaṃ prati me
children.translated_text: Before my friends, toward my beloved bowed in front of me while the flow of speech and feeling is obstructed,

children.text: srotasa iva nimnaṃ prati rāgasya dviguṇa āvegaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the current of passion has a doubled force, like a stream toward a low place.

children.text: rūpam idaṃ kāntir asāv ayam utkarṣaḥ suvarṇaracaneyam
children.translated_text: This is beauty, that is radiance, this is excellence, this is a construction of gold.
Graceful one, joined with a poor man, you wander at the doorway of every house.
Into a beggar's bowl made of leaves from the bower, contemptuously she gives food,
though stale, made warm and bitter by her hot, sharp sighs.

children.text: rakṣati na khalu nijasthitim alaghuḥ sthāpayati nāyakaḥ sa yathā
children.translated_text: As that not-light lord does not protect his own position but establishes another,
so this necklace-string, pierced by his qualities, remains exactly in that state.
Slender-limbed woman, you shine like an auspicious water-jar with a mango shoot,
your face kissed by that very first-risen passion.
A young woman who can be won by one devoid of beauty and virtues becomes light, like dust fickle in the wind.

children.text: prathayati pṛghuguṇaneyā taruṇī taraṇir iva garimāṇam ||
children.translated_text: But one led by many virtues makes her dignity known, like a boatman his boat's weight.
When fresh passion opens out, O slow, slower, slowest-eyed woman in the course of separation,

children.text: sasmitasalajjam īkṣitam idam iṣṭaṃ siddham ācaṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: this smiling and bashful glance announces that what was desired has been accomplished.

children.text: roṣo 'pi rasavatīnāṃ na karkaśo vā cirānubandhī vā
children.translated_text: Even the anger of women rich in rasa is neither harsh nor long-lasting.

children.text: varṣāṇām upalo 'pi hi susnigdhaḥ kṣaṇikakalpaś ca ||
children.translated_text: For even the hailstones of the rains are very moist and almost momentary.

children.text: rodanam etad dhanyaṃ sakhi kiṃ bahu mṛtyur api mamānarghaḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, this weeping is blessed; why say much? Even my death would be beyond price,
for it was caused by him, as if by a dream, captivating to the eyes.

children.text: roṣeṇaiva mayā sakhi vakro 'pi granthilo 'pi kaṭhino 'pi
children.translated_text: Friend, merely by my anger, though crooked, knotted, and hard,

children.text: ṛjutām anīyatāyaṃ sadyaḥ svedena vaṃśa iva ||
children.translated_text: this man was at once brought to straightness by sweat, like a bamboo.

children.text: rajanīm iyam upanetuṃ pitṛprasūḥ prathamam upatasthe
children.translated_text: To bring on the night, this mother of her father first approached;
she herself colors the moon, a bad leader, like a wicked procuress.

children.text: lagnāsi kṛṣṇavartmani susnigdhe varti hanta dagdhāsi
children.translated_text: You have clung to a black path, O wick, very oily; alas, you have been burned.

children.text: ayam akhilanayanasubhago nu bhuktamuktāṃ punaḥ spṛśati ||
children.translated_text: Does this one, delightful to every eye, touch again what has been enjoyed and abandoned?

children.text: lakṣmīḥ śikṣayati guṇān amūn punar durgatir vidhūnayati
children.translated_text: Prosperity teaches these virtues, but misfortune shakes them away again;

children.text: pūrṇo bhavati suvṛttas tuṣārarucir apacaye vakraḥ ||
children.translated_text: only when full is he well-rounded and pleasing with frostlike radiance; in waning he is crooked.
The empty house, its doorway blocked by cut spider-threads and with moths falling,
seems to weep, friend, when that traveler departs, its face covered by the hem of its garment.
Clinging to her very broad hips, where the play of an elephant's trunk is imagined,

children.text: vapre saktaṃ dvipam iva śṛṅgāras tvāṃ vibhūṣayati ||
children.translated_text: love adorns you like an elephant stuck on a rampart.

children.text: liptaṃ na mukhaṃ nāṅgaṃ na pakṣatī na caraṇāḥ parāgeṇa
children.translated_text: The face is not smeared, nor the body, nor the wings, nor the feet with pollen;
as if not touching the lotus at all, the clever bee has drunk the honey.

children.text: lagnaṃ jaghane tasyāḥ śuṣyati nakhalakṣma mānasaṃ ca mama
children.translated_text: The nail-mark clinging to her hip is drying up, and so is my mind;
this enjoyment was unclear, unperceived, full of deeper passion and distress.
To shame <s>Madhudviṣ</s>, whose heart has been drunk by all the cowherd women, <s>Rādhā</s>,
as if ignorant, asks the tale of <s>Śambhu</s>, satisfied by half his beloved.
The beauties on the shore of the milk-ocean sing the praises of <s>Rādhā</s>,
whose arms are the essence of the milk-ocean condensed by the fire of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s sighs.

children.text: līlāgārasya bahiḥ sakhīṣu caraṇātithau mayi priyayā
children.translated_text: Outside the pleasure-house, while I was a guest at her feet among her friends, by my beloved
favor was openly shown when she gave me the fan at the window.

children.text: varṇahṛtir na lalāṭe na lulitam aṅgaṃ na cādhare daṃśaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no loss of color on the forehead, the body is not disheveled, and there is no bite on the lip;

children.text: utpalam ahāri vāri ca na spṛṣṭam upāyacatureṇa ||
children.translated_text: the lotus was stolen, but the water was not touched by the one skilled in stratagems.
On the beloved's chest, uneven with countless wounds from many weapons,

children.text: śrīr api vīravadhūr api garvotpulakā sukhaṃ svapiti ||
children.translated_text: both <s>Śrī</s> and the hero's bride sleep happily, thrilled with pride.
Even when you turn away, your breaths, released like arrows by an unfair archer of Love,

children.text: bhindanti pṛṣṭhapatitāḥ priya hṛdayaṃ mama tava śvāsāḥ ||
children.translated_text: falling on my back, O beloved, pierce my heart.

children.text: vyaktam adhunā sametaḥ khaṇḍo madirākṣi daśanavasane te
children.translated_text: Now it is clear, wine-eyed one: a piece has met the garment of your teeth;

children.text: yan navasudhaikasāre lobhini tat kim api nādrākṣam ||
children.translated_text: since, greedy girl, in that one essence of fresh nectar, I did not see some certain thing.
As the two young lovers fan one another, all their limbs are separated,

children.text: sanmaitrīva śroṇī paraṃ nidāghe'pi na vighaṭitā ||
children.translated_text: but the hips, like true friendship, are not parted even in the heat.

children.text: vyāroṣaṃ māninyās tamo divaḥ kāsaraṃ kalam abhūmeḥ
children.translated_text: The dawn twilight drives away the proud woman's anger, the darkness from the sky, the buffalo from the mire of earth,
and the bee bound by the lotus.

children.text: vakṣasi vijṛmbhamāṇe stanabhinnaṃ truṭati kañcukaṃ tasyāḥ
children.translated_text: As her breast expands, the bodice split by her breasts bursts apart;

children.text: pūrvadayitānurāgas tava hṛdi na manāg api truṭati ||
children.translated_text: but your affection for a former beloved does not burst even slightly in your heart.

children.text: vyaktim avekṣya tad anyāṃ tasyām eveti viditam adhunā tu
children.translated_text: Seeing a manifestation elsewhere, I now know that it is there in her alone;

children.text: harmyaharimukham iva tvām ubhayoḥ sādhāraṇaṃ vedmi ||
children.translated_text: like the lion-faced spout of a mansion, I regard you as common to both.
By the comings and goings of you, who remove heat, as of a fan nearby,

children.text: añcalam iva cañcalatāṃ mama sakhyāḥ prāpitaṃ cetaḥ ||
children.translated_text: my friend's mind has been brought to flutter like the hem of a garment.

children.text: vitarantī rasam antar mamārdrabhāvaṃ tanoṣi tanugātri
children.translated_text: Slender-limbed one, though you give rasa within, you make my moist feeling grow,

children.text: antaḥsalilā sarid iva yan nivasasi bahir adṛśyāpi ||
children.translated_text: because, like an underground river, you dwell inside though unseen outside.
A proud man, having made many attachments and been scorned by a woman high with pride,

children.text: labhate kutaḥ prabodhaṃ sa jāgaritvaiva nidrāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: how can he gain awakening, since he sleeps while remaining awake?
Fearing that her beloved is turned away through shame and devoid of affection, sweet with pleading words,
the young girl casts a glance, wet with love and guilty, toward him.
Fine-bodied girl, while he loves your breast, breathes heavily, is a hero only in words, and sweats profusely,
stand with your forehead pressed to his forehead; you are conquered.
As <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> moves all around while <s>Rādhā</s>'s eyes are restless with passion,
the uneven-arrowed Love makes an arrow purified by piercing the ten directions.
When four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> turned away and even <s>Īśa</s> had taken on helplessness,
only <s>Hari</s>, in rescuing the submerged earth, became stiff-haired with horripilation.
Dwelling on the bank of a pond, thorny fences, and wakeful bees: below these,

children.text: ketakaviṭapa kim etair nanu vāraya mañjarīgandham ||
children.translated_text: ketaka branch, why bother? Surely restrain the fragrance of your blossom-cluster.

children.text: vicalasi mugdhe vidhṛtā yathā tathā viśasi hṛdayamadaye me
children.translated_text: You tremble, innocent girl, and, held just as you are, you enter my pitiless heart,
like the power of the flower-bowed god touching a trembling target.
Having made war with an unequal arrow, having conquered the splendor of <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, and making a display,

children.text: puruṣāyite virājati dehas tava sakhi śikhaṇḍīva ||
children.translated_text: your body, friend, shines in the woman-on-top posture like <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>.
When someone drinks the honey of a woman's bimba-like lower lip through the gap in the fence,
even the lord of the gods, despising nectar, longs for it.
She shines among many flowers, in the honey perfumed by women, in the ear-ornament, and in the head-ornament of young men,
like a bee among forest blossoms.

children.text: vrīḍāprasaraḥ prathamaṃ tad anu ca rasabhāvapuṣṭaceṣṭeyam
children.translated_text: First there is a spread of modesty, and then these gestures strengthened by the feeling of rasa;

children.text: javanīvinirgamād anu naṭīva dayitā mano harati ||
children.translated_text: after emerging from behind the curtain, like an actress, the beloved steals the mind.

children.text: vāsasi haridrayeva tvayi gaurāṅgyā niveśito rāgaḥ
children.translated_text: The passion placed in you by the fair-limbed woman is like turmeric on a garment;
that was suddenly removed by the informer, like falling water.
O deer, because you are to be tormented by the tiger of passion, blinded by fragrance spreading everywhere,

children.text: kvacid api kuraṅga bhavato nābhīm ādāya na sthānam ||
children.translated_text: there is no place at all for you anywhere once your musk-navel has been taken.
Among the banyan, kuṭaja, śāla, śālmali, mango, bahusāra, and sindhuvāra trees,
there is distinction, even when they share the fragrance born from Mount <s>Malaya</s>.
Leaving <s>Śaṅkara</s>, though the tip of his matted hair was set down for you, because of the fault of fickleness,

children.text: vaṭam ekam anusarantī jāhnavi luṭhasi prayāgataṭe ||
children.translated_text: you follow a single banyan, <s>Jāhnavī</s>, and roll about on the bank at <s>Prayāga</s>.

children.text: veda caturṇāṃ kṣaṇadā praharāṇāṃ saṅgamaṃ viyogaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The night knows the meeting and separation of the four watches,

children.text: caraṇānām iva kūrmī saṅkocam api prasāram api ||
children.translated_text: just as a female tortoise knows both the contraction and the extension of her feet.

children.text: vṛtivivareṇa viśantī subhaga tvām īkṣituṃ sakhīdṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: Entering through a gap in the fence in order to look at you, handsome one, your friend's glance
steals the cage of a young man's heart, like an arrow of <s>Manmatha</s> lodged within it.
Skilled appraiser, do not reckon this one as equal to the scale of the marketplace:

children.text: dharmaghaṭo 'sāv adharīkaroti laghum upari nayati gurum ||
children.translated_text: that is the scale of <s>dharma</s> (merit); it lowers the light man and raises the weighty one.

children.text: vāsaragamyam anūror ambaram avanī ca vāmanaikapadam
children.translated_text: The sky can be traversed in a day by <s>Anūru</s>, and the earth by one step of <s>Vāmana</s>;

children.text: jaladhir api potalaṅghyaḥ satāṃ manaḥ kena tulayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the ocean can be crossed by a boat; by what measure shall we weigh the mind of the good?
Deer-eyed girl, the stars shine in the sky, clear in the lap of night marked by long streaks of darkness,
like clusters of letters written on a leaf.
The teacher <s>Manobhava</s>, expert in the varied bendings of the limbs,
makes the young girl, his new pupil, dance on the bed by the method of love, as if with a cane-creeper.

children.text: viparītam api rataṃ te sroto nadyā ivānukūlam idam
children.translated_text: Even your reversed lovemaking is favorable to me, like the current of a river;

children.text: taṭatarum iva mama hṛdayaṃ samūlam api vegato harati ||
children.translated_text: it sweeps away my heart, root and all, with force, like a tree on the bank.

children.text: vaibhavabhājāṃ dūṣaṇam api bhūṣaṇapakṣa eva nikṣiptam
children.translated_text: For those endowed with greatness, even a blemish is placed on the side of ornament;

children.text: ugṇam ātmanām adharmaṃ dveṣaṃ ca gṛṇanti kāṇādāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Kāṇādas</s> declare both the harsh quality of selves and their aversion to <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
Crooked, falsely tender, dark, and clinging near the ear:

children.text: kaṃ vañcayanti na sakhe khalāś ca gaṇikākaṭākṣāś ca ||
children.translated_text: whom do villains not deceive, friend, and whom do the side-glances of courtesans not deceive?
From within the belly of a cloud-vessel encircled by the blaze of lightning,
beloved, hailstones come out together with the rain, stealing the radiance of pure boiled rice.

children.text: vyajanādibhir upacāraiḥ kiṃ marupathikasya gṛhiṇi vihitair me
children.translated_text: Housewife, what use to me, a desert traveler, are services performed with fans and the like?
My heat finds peace between the pair of plantain-trees that are your thighs.

children.text: vaiguṇye'pi hi mahatā vinirmitaṃ bhavati karma śobhāyai
children.translated_text: Even with a defect, an act fashioned by the great becomes beautiful;
the dance of a broad-hipped woman charms, though it is made slow by her heavy hips.

children.text: vīkṣya satīnāṃ gaṇane rekhām ekāṃ tayā svanāmāṅkām
children.translated_text: When, in the counting of chaste women, she saw one line marked with her own name,

children.text: santu yuvāno hasituṃ svayam evāpāri nāvaritum ||
children.translated_text: let the young men laugh; she herself could not manage to stop laughing.
Your body is like Mount <s>Vindhya</s>, with hips like the <s>Narmadā</s> full of many whirlpools;
it checks the movement even of a sage, as if capable of halting the chariot of the sun.
Breaker of fences, capable of trampling, utterly uncontrolled, playground of bad conduct,
greedy for hundreds of other enclosures, wicked bull, do you remember your own home too?

children.text: vaṃśāvalambanaṃ yad yo vistāro guṇasya yāvanatiḥ
children.translated_text: That support from lineage, that extent of virtue, that bending down,
belong to both a net and a villain, and lead to the destruction of what sleeps in their own lap.
On the peak of Mount <s>Vindhya</s>, the wind sharpens the rows of clouds into sword-blades,
with the light of rising lightning, solely for the killing of travelers.
First, the footstep of me as I arrived, dusty from her hanging braid, was washed with tears

children.text: āyātasya padaṃ mama gehinyā tad anu salilena ||
children.translated_text: by my housewife, and only afterward with water.

children.text: vakṣaḥsthalasupte mama mukham upadhātuṃ na maulim ālabhase
children.translated_text: When, exhausted from love, you try to place your face upon my chest as I lie there, you cannot reach my head,
for it has been pushed far away by the weight of your full, high breasts.
Messenger, by bringing affectionate conciliation within the business of your mouth,
you are the fang of that snake-like man, meant for the ruin of virtuous women.

children.text: śrīr api bhujaṅgabhoge mohanavijñena śīlitā yena
children.translated_text: If even <s>Hari</s>, by whom <s>Śrī</s> was accustomed to the enjoyment of the serpent and who is skilled in enchantment,

children.text: so 'pi hariḥ puruṣo yadi puruṣā itare'pi kiṃ kurmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is a man, then what are we to do if the others too are men?

children.text: śaṅke yā sthairyamayī ślathayati bāhū manobhavasyāpi
children.translated_text: I suspect that you, made of firmness, loosen even the arms of <s>Manobhava</s>;

children.text: darpaśilām iva bhavatīṃ kataras taruṇo vicālayati ||
children.translated_text: what young man could move you, like a slab of stone proud in its hardness?
Fragile as a tiger's claw, though fashioned of very hard gold,

children.text: bālānām api bālāsāyasyās tvam api hṛdi vasasi ||
children.translated_text: you still dwell in my heart, as hard to attain even for young girls as childish hope itself.

children.text: śruta eva śrutihāriṇi rāgotkarṣeṇa kaṇṭham adhivasati
children.translated_text: Merely heard, O ear-stealing one, it dwells in the throat through excess of passion;

children.text: gīta iva tvayi madhure karoti nārthagrahaṃ sutanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: in you, sweet as a song, the slender woman makes no grasping of meaning.
<s>Śrī</s> gained slight likeness through the śrī-fruit, and kingship through the king of grasses;
but because of the full likeness of your breasts, the pot has attained universal sovereignty.

children.text: śroṇī bhūmāv aṅke priyo bhayaṃ manasi patibhuje mauliḥ
children.translated_text: Her hips on the ground, her beloved in her lap, fear in her mind, her head on her husband's arm,

children.text: gūḍhaśvāso vadane suratam idaṃ cet tṛṇaṃ tridivam ||
children.translated_text: and hidden breath in her mouth: if this is lovemaking, then heaven is mere grass.

children.text: śliṣyann iva cumbann iva paśyann iva collikhann ivātṛptaḥ
children.translated_text: As if embracing, as if kissing, as if gazing, as if scratching, still unsatisfied,

children.text: dadhad iva hṛdayasyāntaḥ smarāmi tasyā muhur jaghanam ||
children.translated_text: as if holding it inside my heart, I remember her hips again and again.

children.text: śirasi caraṇaprahāraṃ pradāya niḥsāryatāṃ sa te tad api
children.translated_text: Let that snake-like man be driven out after giving him a kick on the head; even so,

children.text: cakrāṅkito bhujaṅgaḥ kāliya iva sumukhi kālindyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fair-faced one, he is marked with a discus, like <s>Kāliya</s> from the <s>Kālindī</s> river.

children.text: śocyaiva sā kṛśāṅgī bhūtimayī bhavatu guṇamayī vāpi
children.translated_text: That slender woman is indeed to be pitied, whether she is made of ashes or made of virtues,

children.text: snehaikavaśya bhavatā tyaktā dīpena vartir iva ||
children.translated_text: for, obedient only to affection, she has been abandoned by you like a wick by a lamp.
Growing day by day, like a parrot in a cage made of wooden bars,
my grief, sharp-faced as <s>Smara</s>'s arrow, cuts the heart of my beloved.
Having heard of the sudden death of the young parrot, the sole treasure of all delight,
the traveler understood the loss of the housewife's modesty only when he arrived.
Though she had been accustomed to the enjoyment of the serpent and was lifted up in his lap by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: acalaiva kīrtyate bhūḥ kim aśakyaṃ nāma vasumatyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the earth is still celebrated as unmoving: what, after all, is impossible for <s>Vasumatī</s>?

children.text: śyāmā vilocanaharī bāleyaṃ manasi hanta sajantī
children.translated_text: This dark young girl, stealing the eyes, alas, fastening herself in his mind,
tears away the former wife like a tendril of smoke erasing a wall-painting.

children.text: śataśo gatir āvṛttiḥ śataśaḥ kaṇṭhāvalambanaṃ śataśaḥ
children.translated_text: Hundreds of times her going, hundreds of times her turning back, hundreds of times her clinging to my neck,

children.text: śataśo yāmīti vacaḥ smarāmi tasyāḥ pravāsadine ||
children.translated_text: hundreds of times her words, "I am going"--I remember all this from the day of her departure.
Asked by the cowherd women, who had heard the call of the cuckoos, about what he desired, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
with his eyes fixed on their breasts, gives his approved answer through the thunder of his flute.
O digit of the moon, do not carry pride, thinking, "My foot is placed on <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s head";
the result of this for you will be being wiped by the dust of <s>Caṇḍī</s>'s feet.
On the tip of a branch, content in a nest swung by the wind, dwells
a pair of birds whose only refuge is karma, heedless of danger, unrelaxed in play.
O parrot, <s>Nārada</s> of the battle of love, all-knowing one, sole essence of the heart's secret,
mute before elders, be gracious: split the jambu fruit.

children.text: śirasā vahasi kapardaṃ rudra ruditvāpi rajatam arjayasi
children.translated_text: You carry matted hair on your head, O <s>Rudra</s>; even after weeping you acquire silver.

children.text: asyāpy udarasyārdhaṃ bhajatas tava vetti kas tattvam ||
children.translated_text: But when this belly of yours shares half its body with her too, who knows your true nature?
You are only to be heard, like nectar; only to be seen from afar, like the white-rayed digit of the moon.

children.text: duṣṭabhujaṅgaparīte tvaṃ ketaki na khalu naḥ spṛśyā ||
children.translated_text: Surrounded by wicked snakes, O ketakī, you are certainly not to be touched by us.
By you, who bowed and offered flowers, with virtues brought to my ears,
I have been brought under control, O go-between, as if by the creeper-bow of Love.
O cry honored by śākhoṭaka, śākhoṭaja, vaikhānasa, and karaṭa, sound for a long time;

children.text: nādarapadam iha gaṇakāḥ pramāṇapuruṣo bhavān ekaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the astrologers here are not worthy of respect; you alone are the authoritative man.
For you, whose beauty is like a streak of moonlight, now gone to another man's hand in marriage,
it harms the beauty of your limbs as if you were the little sword of Love.

children.text: śaithilyena bhṛtā api bhartuḥ kāryaṃ tyajanti na suvṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Even when borne loosely, well-rounded women do not abandon their husband's task;
when the strong arm is pulled, the bracelets jingle and run along.
Having abandoned his weapon, occupied by six-footed insects and filled with pollen-dust,

children.text: tvāṃ muṣṭimeyamadhyām adhunā śaktiṃ smaro vahati ||
children.translated_text: Love now bears you as his spear, with a waist measurable by a fist.
She, under the pretext of duties fit for the day, is only the housewife;

children.text: dvitither divasasya parā tithir iva sevyā niśi tvam asi ||
children.translated_text: but you are to be enjoyed at night, like the later lunar date after the second day.
The mass of your sweat-drops, hanging on the fresh nail-scratches of your breasts,
shines like a stream of pearls entering a silk thread.

children.text: saubhāgyagarvam ekā karotu yūthasya bhūṣaṇaṃ kariṇī
children.translated_text: Let one cow-elephant alone show the pride of good fortune, the ornament of the herd:

children.text: atyāyām avator yā madāndhayor madhyam adhivasati ||
children.translated_text: she who, in danger at the ford, dwells between two elephants blinded with rut.
Having inferred from the pain in my own feet the ache in your head, and with jealousy humbled,

children.text: aparāddhā subhaga tvāṃ svayam aham anunetum āyātā ||
children.translated_text: though I was the offender, O fortunate one, I have come myself to conciliate you.
What can even the oilman do with his wheel while pressing things full of oil?

children.text: cālayati pārthivān api yaḥ sa kulālaḥ paraṃ cakrī ||
children.translated_text: But the potter, who moves even earthly kings, is the supreme wheel-bearer.

children.text: sarale na veda bhavatī bahubhaṅgā bahurasā bahuvivartā
children.translated_text: Simple girl, you do not know the course of unchaste women's eyes, of loves, and of rivers:
full of many bends, many flavors, and many turns.
Friend, the shadow, oppressed by the doubled ranks of the midday sun's rays,
takes shelter all around the root of the tree, as if to plunge into the basin.

children.text: sakhi śṛṇu mama priyo 'yaṃ gehaṃ yenaiva vartmanāyātaḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, listen: by whatever road this beloved of mine came home,
he asks other men arriving together about the cities, villages, and rivers on that route.

children.text: sāyaṃ ravir analam asau madanaśaraṃ sa ca viyoginīcetaḥ
children.translated_text: At evening the sun enters fire; that fire enters the arrow of Love; and that arrow enters the heart of the separated woman.

children.text: idam api tamaḥsamūhaṃ so 'pi nabho nirbharaṃ viśati ||
children.translated_text: This mass of darkness too enters that, and that in turn fills the sky completely.
Like a conch filled at the time of Love's battle, with its throat-stalk twice as thick,
the pigeon coos on top of the ruined palace, as if eager to conquer.
This weeping--with quivering lip, ceaseless tears, breasts trembling as the voice is checked,
and the face placed on hands set upon the knees--belongs to a naturally compliant woman.

children.text: svayam upanītair aśanaiḥ puṣṇantī nīḍanirvṛtaṃ dayitam
children.translated_text: Feeding her beloved, content in the nest, with food brought by herself,
let the female crane, knowing the innate flavor of love, bear the pride of a fortunate woman.

children.text: svarasena badhnatāṃ karam ādāne kaṇṭakotkarais tudatām
children.translated_text: Though they bind the hand with their own juice when being taken, and pierce it with heaps of thorns,
even the enjoyment of the pods of treacherous jackfruits is not to be trusted.

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ dākṣiṇyān nety upadiṣṭaṃ hareṇa taruṇīnām
children.translated_text: By <s>Hara</s>, placing the left half of the goddess in the sculpture of his own body,
young women were instructed that good fortune does not come from compliance.

children.text: subhaga svabhavanabhittau bhavatā saṃmardya pīḍitā sutanuḥ
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, the slender girl was crushed and pained by you against the wall of your own house;

children.text: sā pīḍayaiva jīvati dadhatī vaidyeṣu vidveṣam ||
children.translated_text: she lives by that very pain, while bearing hatred toward physicians.
That slender girl, made of strands, naturally clear, dependent on the grasp of the hand,
was whirled by you, knower of many mantras, like a Kashmiri rosary.
Blessed with a bashful smile, touched and yet as if untouched, moving a little away,

children.text: apasarasi sundari yathā yathā tathā spṛśasi mama hṛdayam ||
children.translated_text: however you withdraw, beautiful one, in just that way you touch my heart.

children.text: sakhi sukhayaty avakāśaprāptaḥ preyān yathā tathā na gṛhī
children.translated_text: Friend, a lover who has gained an opening gives pleasure in a way a husband does not;

children.text: vātād avāritād api bhavati gavākṣānilaḥ śītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even more than unobstructed wind, the breeze from a window is cool.

children.text: satatam aruṇitamukhe sakhi nigirantī garalam iva girāṃ gumpham
children.translated_text: Friend, with your face always reddened, swallowing as if poison this cluster of words,
O serpent-woman, scorning medicines and mantras, you dye the red still redder.
With the charming body of a land-lotus and one alarmed leg set in its lap,
on the bank of the lotus-pond the lotus-fiber-necked bird reassures the fish.
Having made the root of the navel, marked by nails and exceedingly fair, bare of clothing,

children.text: anayā sevita pavana tvaṃ kiṃ kṛtamalayabhṛgupātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Served by her, O wind, why have you hurled yourself down from the slope of <s>Malaya</s>?

children.text: sarvāṅgam arpayantī lolā suptaṃ śrameṇa śayyāyām
children.translated_text: Offering all her limbs, restless, asleep on the bed from fatigue,

children.text: alasam api bhāgyavantaṃ bhajate puruṣayiteva śrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> attends even a fortunate man who is sluggish, like a woman taking the man's role.

children.text: suditaṃ tad eva yatra smāraṃ smāraṃ viyogaduḥkhāni
children.translated_text: That alone was a happy day, when, remembering again and again the sorrows of separation,

children.text: āliṅgati sā gāḍhaṃ punaḥ punar yāminīprathame ||
children.translated_text: she embraced me tightly, again and again, at the beginning of the night.

children.text: sāntarbhayaṃ bhujiṣyā yathā yathācarati samadhikāṃ sevām
children.translated_text: As a maidservant, with hidden fear, performs ever greater service in whatever way,
so, in just that way, his housewife becomes suspicious, jealous, and afraid.

children.text: sundari darśayati yathā bhavadvipakṣasya tatsakhī kāntim
children.translated_text: Lovely one, just as that friend of your rival shows off her beauty,

children.text: patati tathā mama dṛṣṭis tvadekadāsasya sāsūyā ||
children.translated_text: so my gaze, I who am solely your servant, falls upon her with jealousy.
With signs under her control: wounds on the lips, nail-marks, letters, and sleep robbed away,

children.text: subhagā subhagety anayā sakhi nikhilā mukharitā pallī ||
children.translated_text: friend, by this woman the whole village has been made to resound, 'fortunate, fortunate indeed!'

children.text: sarita iva yasya gehe śuṣyanti viśālagotrajā nāryaḥ
children.translated_text: In whose house women born of great families dry up like rivers,

children.text: kṣārāsv eva sa tṛpyati jalanidhilaharīṣu jalada iva ||
children.translated_text: he is satisfied only among briny ocean-waves, like a cloud.
O sole ornament of the whole encampment, peak-toothed one, whose heart has grown hard,

children.text: giribhuva iva tava manye manaḥ śilā samabhavaccaṇḍi ||
children.translated_text: I think your mind, fierce woman, has become a rock-crystal of the mountain-land.
Friend, hard to fathom and deep, doing harm even to the beloved,

children.text: khala iva durlakṣyas tava vinatamukhasyopari sthitaḥ kopaḥ ||
children.translated_text: your anger, like a villain, is hard to recognize as it rests above your downcast face.
Bathed in sweat with her garment, walking seven circles as if the seven steps,
lovely, altered by the fire of passion, ashamed, she bows down.
This gathering of men of the same meter, proceeding with good rasa,
has been broken the moment men of different meter arrived, like the creation of a poem.

children.text: sarvāsām eva sakhe paya iva surataṃ manohāri
children.translated_text: Friend, intercourse with all women is charming, like milk,

children.text: tasyā eva punaḥ punar āvṛttau dugdham iva madhuram ||
children.translated_text: but with her alone, when repeated again and again, it is sweet like milk boiled down.

children.text: svapne'pi yāṃ na muñcasi yā te'nugrāhiṇī hṛdisthāpi
children.translated_text: Even in a dream you do not leave her, who favors you and dwells in your heart,

children.text: duṣṭāṃ na buddhim iva tāṃ gūḍhavyabhicāriṇīṃ vetsi ||
children.translated_text: yet you do not know that she is secretly unfaithful, like a wicked thought.
Moving with a covering, like a whirlwind with grass, O woman of flawless limbs,

children.text: harasi kṣipasi taralayasi bhramayasi tolayasi pātayasi ||
children.translated_text: you steal, fling, make tremble, whirl, weigh, and cast down my mind.

children.text: sā bahulakṣaṇabhāvā strīmātraṃ veti kitava tava tulyam
children.translated_text: Whether she is a woman of many signs and emotions or merely a woman, gambler, it is all the same to you:

children.text: koṭir varāṭikā vā dyūtavidheḥ sarva eva paṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether a crore or a cowrie, in the rule of dice every stake is just a stake.

children.text: sā virahadahanadūnā mṛtvā mṛtvāpi jīvati varākī
children.translated_text: Burned by the fire of separation, the poor woman lives even after dying again and again,
like a gaming-piece, gambler, made favorable to you after the dice have been thrown.

children.text: sparśād eva svedaṃ janayati na ca me dadāti nidrātum
children.translated_text: By mere touch the hot season makes me sweat, and it does not allow me to sleep;

children.text: pirya iva jaghanāṃśukam api na nidāghaḥ kṣaṇam api kṣamate ||
children.translated_text: like a beloved woman's hip-cloth, it cannot endure even for a moment.

children.text: sā bhavato bhāvanayā samayaviruddhaṃ manobhavaṃ bālā
children.translated_text: Through contemplation of you, young woman, out of season, bears the fruit of love,
O handsome one, like a fresh creeper through the power of dohada.

children.text: spṛśati nakhair na ca vilikhati sicayaṃ gṛhṇāti na ca vimocayati
children.translated_text: She touches with her nails but does not scratch, takes hold of the garment but does not release it;

children.text: na ca muñcati na ca madayati nayati niśāṃ sā na nidrāti ||
children.translated_text: she neither lets go nor intoxicates me: she passes the night, and she does not sleep.

children.text: stanajaghanadvayam asyā laṅghitamadhyaḥ sakhe mama kaṭākṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, my glance, devoted to the pair of her breasts and hips, crossing over the middle,
does not abandon the two banks of that river, like a crow at a ford.
Saying with a bashful smile and gentle sighing, 'Do not, do not touch me,'

children.text: ākopam etya vātāyanaṃ pidhāya sthitaṃ priyayā ||
children.translated_text: my beloved came to anger, shut the window, and stood there.
With hand-grasping, with weeping, with reproach, with nail and fist, eager to conquer:
her lovemaking is true lovemaking; another is merely a Prajāpati sacrifice.

children.text: sakhi na khalu nimalānāṃ vidadhaty abhidhānam api mukhe malināḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, the impure certainly do not place even the name of the pure in their mouth.
Who has ever heard any sound from cuckoos other than 'kuhū'?

children.text: svalpā iti rāmabalair ye nyastā nāśaye payorāśeḥ
children.translated_text: Those mountains which, by <s>Rāma</s>'s troops, were set down in the ocean as small,

children.text: te śailāḥ sthitimanto hanta laghimnaiva bahumānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: stood firm there; alas, respect came precisely through lightness.
That dark, slender woman, burned by separation intensified through cooling treatment,
has been brought to pallor, like dūrvā grass by frost.
Friend, she did not grow so intoxicated when sprinkled by the steady stream of water from the hand of her carefully watching beloved,

children.text: sotkampena mayā sakhi dṛṣṭā sā mādyati sma yathā ||
children.translated_text: as she did when she was looked at by me with trembling.

children.text: sakhi moghīkṛtamadane pativrate kas tavādaraṃ kurute
children.translated_text: Friend, who pays regard to a chaste wife in whom desire has been made futile?

children.text: nāśrauṣīr bhagavān api sa kāmaviddho haraḥ pūjyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Have you not heard that even blessed <s>Hara</s> is worshipful because he was pierced by <s>Kāma</s>?

children.text: sā mayi na dāsabuddhir na ratir nāpi trapā na viśvāsaḥ
children.translated_text: In her toward me there is no servant's attitude, no passion, no shame, and no trust.

children.text: hanta nirīkṣya navoḍhāṃ manye vayam apiryā jātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alas, having looked at the newly married girl, I think we have become unlovely.

children.text: sucirāyāte gṛhiṇī niśi bhuktā dinamukhe vidagdheyam
children.translated_text: When the housewife has arrived very late and has been enjoyed by night, this clever woman at daybreak
does not show her own body, marked by white nail-scratches and wet with saffron.
Clinging to the breasts, hips, and thighs, deeply attached, with affection set in place:

children.text: priya kālapariṇatir iyaṃ virajyase yan nakhāṅka iva ||
children.translated_text: beloved, this is the ripening of time, that you lose color like a nail-mark.

children.text: sā vicchāyā niśi niśi sutanur bahutuhinaśītale talpe
children.translated_text: That slender woman, pale night after night on a couch very cold with much frost,

children.text: jvalati tvadīyavirahād oṣadhir iva himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe ||
children.translated_text: burns from separation from you, like a medicinal plant on the back of <s>Himavat</s>.

children.text: sā nīrase tava hṛdi praviśati niryāti na labhate sthairyam
children.translated_text: She enters your flavorless heart and comes out again; she finds no stability there,
handsome one, my friend, like a line of moonlight on the disk of the sun.

children.text: sukumāratvaṃ kāntir nitāntasāratvam āntarāś ca guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Tenderness, beauty, extreme substantiality, and inner virtues:

children.text: kiṃ nāma nendulekhe śaśagraheṇaiva tava kathitam ||
children.translated_text: what indeed has not been declared about you, crescent-moon-like one, by that very hare-mark?
For those whose minds care only for fragrance, let there be no special distinction in the sandalwood tree of <s>Malaya</s>;

children.text: dharmārthināṃ tathāpi sa mṛgyaḥ pūjārtham aśvatthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, for those seeking religious merit, that aśvattha tree is sought for worship.
Just as the wife massages her husband as he lies down, and fans the master of the house,
so the young man is reassured, while his eyes are fixed on the opening of the house-door.

children.text: satyaṃ svalpaguṇeṣu stabdhā sadṛśe punar bhujaṅge sā
children.translated_text: True, she is stiff toward men of slight merit; but when the serpent is her match,
fair one, she bends with her tip lowered, like the staff of <s>Hara</s>'s bow.

children.text: sarvaṃsahāṃ mahīm iva vidhāya tāṃ bāṣpavāribhiḥ pūrṇām
children.translated_text: Having made her like the all-bearing earth, filled with waters of tears,

children.text: bhavanāntaramayam adhunā saṃkrāntas te guruḥ premā ||
children.translated_text: your heavy love has now passed into another house.

children.text: sambhavati na khalu rakṣā sarasānāṃ prakṛticapalacaritānām
children.translated_text: Surely there can be no protection for things full of sap, whose nature and conduct are fickle;
even on <s>Hara</s>'s head, <s>Gaṅgā</s> experiences familiarity with a serpent.
When lotus filaments, ketaka, mango-blossoms, and jasmine flowers are easy to obtain,
the bee, blinded by longing, desires to become the string on <s>Smara</s>'s bow.

children.text: sā lajjitā sapatnī kupitā bhītaḥ priyaḥ sakhī sukhitā
children.translated_text: She was embarrassed, the rival wife angry, the beloved frightened, and the friend delighted,
when the physicians diagnosed the young girl's ailment as wakefulness.
Embracing limb after limb under the pretext of massaging him after his long absence,

children.text: puṣyati ca mānacarcāṃ gṛhiṇī saphalayait cotkalikām ||
children.translated_text: the housewife nourishes the talk of offended pride and also makes her yearning fruitful.

children.text: sā sarvathaiva raktā rāgaṃ guñjeva na tu mukhe vahati
children.translated_text: She is altogether red with passion, like a guñjā berry, but she does not carry that redness on her face;

children.text: vacanapaṭos tava rāgaḥ kevalam āsye śukasyeva ||
children.translated_text: your passion, eloquent one, is only in your mouth, like a parrot's.
Having spent the whole night in lovemaking, fallen between her beloved's arms in the evening,

children.text: uṣasi dadatī pradīpaṃ sakhībhir upahasyate bālā ||
children.translated_text: the young woman, handing over the lamp at dawn, is laughed at by her friends.

children.text: sā tīkṣṇamānadahanā mahataḥ snehasya durlabhaḥ pākaḥ
children.translated_text: She is a sharp fire of offended pride; the ripening of great affection is hard to obtain.

children.text: tvāṃ darvīm iva dūti prayāsayannasmi viśvastaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Messenger, I am trusting you as I trouble you, like a ladle, again and again.
Loss of affection, the will to conquer, battle ending only with the loss of life:

children.text: na vitanute kam anarthaṃ dantini tava yauvanodbhaṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: what disaster does your proud youth not extend, elephant?

children.text: sadanād apaiti dayito hasati sakhī viśati gharaṇim iva bālā
children.translated_text: The beloved leaves the house, the friend laughs, the young woman enters as if into the earth,

children.text: jvalati sapatnī kīre jalpati mugdhe prasīdati ||
children.translated_text: the rival wife blazes, the parrot chatters, and the innocent one is appeased.
Through your favor, frost, I enjoy my beloved as an innocent girl,

children.text: dayitāṃ bhajāmi mugdhām iva tuhina tava prasādena ||
children.translated_text: her body contracted, her garment doubled, and passion stirring only in her mind.

children.text: sakhi lagnaiva vasantī sadāśaye mahati rasamaye tasya
children.translated_text: Friend, though you are constantly attached to him, a great, good-hearted, juicy man,

children.text: bāḍavaśikheva sindhor na manāg apy ārdratāṃ bhajasi ||
children.translated_text: like the submarine fire in the ocean, you do not become even slightly moist.
Friend, this frost-day, after concealing its first delight at sunrise,
torments me at the end, like a barren appointed day.
In the temple, when the young pair had drawn one another's eyes and hearts toward themselves,
the flower raised for worship of the god was offered by each to the other.
At evening, the sound of bees coming out from inside the lotuses
was released by the lotuses like a lament, as they were sorrowful over a friend's misfortune.
Even though the great cause of anger had been created by me myself, she, her thighs trembling,

children.text: na sakhīnām api rudatī mamaiva vakṣaḥsthale patitā ||
children.translated_text: fell weeping not even on her friends, but on my own breast.
Fortunate one, this friend too has grown slack-armed from waving the fan;

children.text: udvartanaṃ na sakhyāḥ samāpyate kiṃcid apagaccha ||
children.translated_text: your friend's rubbing is still not finished; move away a little.
Ashamed at the placing of nails and teeth, angered deeply though newly married,
she has become one whose anger can be managed only by much pleading and grasping of her feet.
With their dark side well taken, light, piercing others, and exceedingly sharp,

children.text: puruṣā api viśikhā api guṇacyutāḥ kasya na bhayāya ||
children.translated_text: both men and arrows, once slipped from the string, are a terror to whom?
By his cheek he made manifest some cause of intoxicated passion;

children.text: dviradasya durjanasya ca madaṃ cakāraiva dānam api ||
children.translated_text: for an elephant and for a wicked man, even giving makes intoxication.

children.text: satyaṃ patir avidagdhaḥ sā tu svadhiyaiva nidhuvane nipuṇā
children.translated_text: True, her husband is unskilled, but she, by her own intelligence, is expert in lovemaking;

children.text: mārttikam ādhāya guruṃ dhanur adhigatam ekalavyena ||
children.translated_text: by setting up a clay teacher, <s>Ekalavya</s> learned the bow.
That proud possessor of good fortune, rejected by you, has been brought to disgrace;
he spreads his own pallor of separation, like a bath in ashes.

children.text: sakhi mama karañjatailaṃ bahusaṃdeśaṃ praheṣyasīty uditā
children.translated_text: When told, 'Friend, you will send my karanja-oil with many messages,'
the unchaste woman hides the tear-water that has come with going to her father-in-law's house.

children.text: saṃdarśayanti sundari kulaṭānāṃ tamasi vitatam avikalpe
children.translated_text: Beautiful one, in the darkness, when there is no alternative, the little lamp of the crest-jewel
on a lover's head, with its wick-like ray, shows courtesans the extended road.

children.text: sarvaṃ vanaṃ tṛṇālyā pihitaṃ pītāḥ sitāṃśuravitārāḥ
children.translated_text: The whole forest is covered by a line of grasses; moon, sun, and stars have been drunk up;
the roads are destroyed by the dark cloud that has risen.

children.text: samyag aniṣpannaḥ san yo 'rthas tvarayā svayaṃ sphuṭīkriyate
children.translated_text: An affair that is not yet properly completed, but is clarified by oneself in haste,

children.text: sa vyaṅga eva bhavati prathamo vinatātanūja iva ||
children.translated_text: becomes malformed indeed, like the first son of <s>Vinatā</s>.

children.text: sajjana eva hi vidyā śobhanāyai bhavati durjane moghā
children.translated_text: Learning is beautiful only in a good person; in a bad person it is useless.
A vulture is not accepted by anyone merely because it sees far.

children.text: subhagaṃ vadati janas taṃ nijapatir iti naiṣa rocate mahyam
children.translated_text: People call him fortunate, saying, 'He is my own husband'; this does not please me.
Even toward nectar, when it has taken the form of medicine, one feels distaste.

children.text: saudhagavākṣagatāpi hi dṛṣṭis taṃ sthitikṛtaprayatnam api
children.translated_text: Even from a palace window, her gaze seizes him, though he strives to keep his place,
like the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, slipped from a peak of the <s>Himālaya</s>, seizing <s>Airāvata</s>.

children.text: sahagharmacāriṇī mama paricchadaḥ sutanu neha sandehaḥ
children.translated_text: Slender one, she is my partner in duty and my household possession; there is no doubt here.
But clinging to me, she does not delight me, like the shade of a parasol on a frosty day.
Abode of every virtue, because of your dwelling among donors, king of trees,
you have become on earth one whose fruit and flowers are not to be accepted by the good.

children.text: sundari tāṭaṅkamayaṃ cakram ivodvahati tāvake karṇe
children.translated_text: Beautiful one, in your ear it bears a wheel made of your earring.
The arrow of her side-glance, intensely sharp and loving <s>Arjuna</s>, falls upon him.
Its abundance of fruit is entirely its own, and its lofty shade is for the sustenance of people;
the life of a good man, like a desert tree, is to be desired merely because it keeps others alive.
To produce burning, bewilderment, and trembling, and even to destroy living beings,

children.text: sakhi durjanasya bhūtiḥ prasarati dūraṃ jvarasyeva ||
children.translated_text: friend, the prosperity of a wicked man spreads far, like a fever.

children.text: sukhayitatarāṃ na rakṣati paricayaleśaṃ gaṇāṅganeva śrīḥ
children.translated_text: Fortune, like a courtesan, does not preserve even the slightest familiarity with one who gives great pleasure;
but the goddess of speech, like a bad mistress, does not leave him, even birth after birth.
Just on seeing, near his own house, a lotus pond with newly born leaves,

children.text: hā gṛhiṇīti pralapaṃś cirāgataḥ sakhi patiḥ patitaḥ ||
