children.translated_text: friend, the husband who had returned after a long time collapsed, crying, 'Ah, my housewife!'

children.text: saci caturānanabhāvād vaimukhyaṃ kvāpi naiva darśayati
children.translated_text: Friend, because he has four faces he never shows aversion anywhere;

children.text: ayam ekahṛdaya eva druhiṇa iva priyatamas tad api ||
children.translated_text: and yet this dearest one, like <s>Druhiṇa</s>, has only one heart.

children.text: satyaṃ madhuro niyataṃ vakro nūnaṃ kalādharo dayitaḥ
children.translated_text: It is true: the beloved is sweet, surely crooked, certainly endowed with digits;

children.text: sa tu veda na dvitīyām akalaṅkaḥ pratipadindur iva ||
children.translated_text: but he knows no second woman, and is stainless, like the moon of the first lunar day.

children.text: svasthānād api vicalati majjati jaladhau ca nīcam api bhajate
children.translated_text: He moves even from his own station, sinks into the ocean, and approaches even what is low;
a good man, intent on protecting his own side, is like Mount <s>Maināka</s>.

children.text: saṃvṛṇu bāṣpajalaṃ sakhi dṛśam uparajyāñjanena valayainām
children.translated_text: Hide the water of your tears, friend; redden this eye with collyrium and bangles,

children.text: dayitaḥ paśyatu pallavapaṅkajayor yugapad eva rucam ||
children.translated_text: so that your beloved may see, all at once, the beauty of a new leaf and a lotus.

children.text: sā pāṇḍudurbalāṅgī nayasi tvaṃ yatra yāti tatraiva
children.translated_text: That pale, weak-limbed woman goes exactly wherever you lead her;
for you, knower of tricks, she is like a knife, mastered merely by taking her by the hand.

children.text: sakhi viśvagañjanīyā lakṣmīr iva kamalamukhi kadaryasya
children.translated_text: Friend, lotus-faced one, like fortune belonging to a miser, you are fit to be mocked by everyone;
for this old man you are useful only for watching and guarding.

children.text: hṛdayajñayā gavākṣe visadṛkṣaṃ kimapi kūjitaṃ sakhyā
children.translated_text: At the window, my friend, knowing my heart, made some strange cooing sound,

children.text: yat kalahabhinnatalpā bhayakapaṭād eti māṃ sutanu ||
children.translated_text: because, slender one, when her bed is split apart by a quarrel, she comes to me under the pretense of fear.

children.text: harati hṛdayaṃ śalākānihito 'ñjanatantur eṣa sakhi mugdhe
children.translated_text: Friend, innocent girl, this streak of collyrium set on the applicator steals the heart;
it is like a mark scratched by the inner brow-bow that shoots arrows from the eyes.

children.text: hasasi caraṇaprahāre talpād apasārito bhuvi svapiṣi
children.translated_text: You laugh when struck by my foot; pushed from the bed, you sleep on the ground;

children.text: nāsadṛśe'pi kṛte priya mama hṛdayāt tvaṃ viniḥsarasi ||
children.translated_text: even when something unworthy is done, beloved, you do not go out from my heart.

children.text: hasati sapatnī śvaśrū roditi vadanaṃ ca pidadhate sakhyaḥ
children.translated_text: The co-wife laughs, the mother-in-law weeps, and the friends cover their faces,
when, as if dreaming, she mutters your name, fortunate man.
Friend, the grief of separation from my beloved, turning over in my heart at every moment,
will violently split it apart, like a line of water splitting an unbaked clay pot.
Alas, separation, with an irresistible and fierce onset, sets me ablaze on every side,

children.text: aruṇas tapanaśilām iva punar na māṃ bhasmatāṃ nayati ||
children.translated_text: yet, like the red sun scorching a sun-stone, it still does not reduce me to ash.

children.text: hṛtvā taṭini taraṅgair bhramitaś cakreṣu nāśaye nihitaḥ
children.translated_text: You have seized me, river, with your waves, whirled me in eddies, placed me in destruction,
and abandoned me in midair like a tree stripped of fruit, leaves, and bark.
On her, whose upper hips have lost the binding of the golden girdle-creeper and who has been enjoyed by another lover,
the line of hair shines like a streak of poison on the breast of <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: kṣīrasya tu dayitatvaṃ yato 'pi śāntopacāram āsādya
children.translated_text: Milk is dear because, even after receiving a soothing treatment,
it makes the body of a mountain bend: what remains of love is like what remains of fever.

children.text: kṣāntam apasārito yac caraṇāvupadhāya supta evāsi
children.translated_text: I forgave you because, though pushed aside, you put my feet beneath your head and fell asleep;

children.text: udghāṭayasi kim ūru niḥśvāsaiḥ pulakayann uṣṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: why now do you uncover my thighs, thrilling them with your hot sighs?

children.text: kṣudrodbhavasya kaṭutāṃ prakaṭayato yacchataśca madam uccaiḥ
children.translated_text: Honey, revealing the sharpness of its low origin and giving intense intoxication,

children.text: madhuno laghupuruṣasya ca garimā laghimā ca bhedāya ||
children.translated_text: and a petty man are distinguished by heaviness and lightness alike.
I worship the goddess of speech, whose mode has already been divided by <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>, <s>Bhavabhūti</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, and the author of the <s>Raghu</s>;

children.text: vāgdevīṃ bhajato mama santaḥ paśyantu ko doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: let good people see what fault there is in me.
Fit to be brought before worthy recipients, rich in good reflections, and full of fresh substance,

children.text: kasya na janayati harṣaṃ satkāvyaṃ madhuravacanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: what person is not delighted by good poetry and by sweet speech?
With a single path, without a second, surpassing, the essence of the worlds, clever with clear expression,
beneficial to the five-arrowed god and to bees, this <s>Saptaśatī</s> is an ornament for the ear.
A lion-roar in the battle of poets, an echo of musical notes, wholly in accord with nectar,
the root of learned men's amusement: this composition has been created by me.
By <s>Udayana</s> and <s>Balabhadra</s>, my pupils and brothers, the <s>Saptaśatī</s>,
like the sky by the sun and moon, has been illuminated after being made pure.
Wise <s>Govardhanācārya</s>, constantly an offering to <s>Hari</s>'s feet, enough to delight the best poets,
has made this <s>Āryāsaptaśatī</s>.
